text: Once upon a time, there was a church in the city. It was very big and tall and looked beautiful in the sunlight. One day, a big truck came by the church and stopped. Someone inside the truck opened the back and began to store lots of boxes in the church. The kids in the neighbourhood were curious and came to have a closer look. Suddenly, the boxes started to move around! They were so excited to see what was inside until they heard a loud sound. The truck driver shouted at them and said it was dangerous and that they should go away. The children were scared, so they ran away into their homes and never came back. The truck driver stored all the boxes safely in the church and then drove away. To this day, no one knows what was inside the boxes and why the driver said it was dangerous.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a boy named Tim. Tim was a happy boy who loved to play with his big red ball. One day, Tim was playing with his ball in the yard. He would throw it high up in the air and catch it. He was having so much fun. Then, Tim had an idea. He wanted to kick the ball as hard as he could. So, he took a big step back and kicked the ball with all his might. The ball flew high and fast, but it went the wrong way! Instead of going to the open yard, the ball went into the house through an open window. Tim ran into the house to find his ball. He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. Then, he heard a loud noise coming from the bathroom. He went to the bathroom and saw his ball inside the toilet! Tim was surprised and said, "Oh no! My ball is in the toilet!" His mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the ball in the toilet and smiled. "Don't worry, Tim," she said. "We can clean the ball and it will be as good as new." So, they cleaned the ball and Tim was happy again. From that day on, Tim made sure to kick the ball only in the yard, away from the house.

One day, a girl named Lucy found a magic seat. This seat was special because it could shrink. Lucy was very excited to try it. She sat on the seat and said, "Shrink, seat, shrink!" And the seat became very small. Lucy was so happy that she wanted to show her friend, Tom. Lucy went to Tom's house and said, "Tom, look at my magic seat! It can shrink!" Tom was very honest and said, "I don't believe you, Lucy. Show me!" So Lucy sat on the seat and said, "Shrink, seat, shrink!" The seat became small again, and Tom was amazed. Together, Lucy and Tom played with the magic seat. They took turns making it shrink and grow. They had so much fun with their new toy. And from that day on, Lucy and Tom became best friends, always honest and kind to each other.

One day, a sweet cat named Kitty went for a walk. The sun was shining bright in the sky. Kitty loved to play outside when the sun shone. She liked to chase butterflies and run in the grass. As Kitty played, she saw a small bird in a cage. The cage was like a jail for the bird. The bird looked sad. Kitty wanted to help the bird. She pushed the cage with her paw, and the door opened. The bird flew away and was very happy. Kitty learned that it was good to help others. She felt happy when she saw the bird fly free. From that day on, Kitty always tried to be kind and help her friends. The sun shone even brighter, and Kitty knew she had done a good thing.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy king. He lived in a big castle. The king loved to measure things. One day, the king went to the park. He saw a big tree. The king wanted to measure the tree. He took out his ruler and started to measure. As the king measured, a big squirrel jumped out of the tree. The king was surprised! The squirrel was friendly and wanted to play. The king forgot about measuring and played with the squirrel all day. They became best friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. The little girl was very smart. She knew how to do many things - like drawing, counting, reading and writing. One day, the little girl made a mistake. Her mommy told her, "That's not a good thing to do. I'm going to have to punish you." She took out a tiny pin and showed it to the little girl. The little girl started to cry. The mommy said, "If you do something wrong, I must punish you. Now, I'm going to give you three pokes with this pin." The little girl was scared, but she hugged her mommy anyway. Then her mommy gave her three pokes with the pin. It hurt a lot! The little girl cried and cried until she went to sleep. It was a bad ending; the little girl never wanted to make a mistake again. From then on, she was very careful.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there were three different animals. A big bear, a small rabbit, and a fast deer. They were best friends and always played together. One day, they found a big tree with many leaves that were starting to fall. The big bear said, "Let's order the leaves by color!" The small rabbit and the fast deer agreed. They started to pick up the leaves and put them in piles. The big bear put the red leaves in one pile, the small rabbit put the yellow leaves in another pile, and the fast deer put the green leaves in the last pile. As they worked together, they saw that the tree looked very pretty with the leaves in different piles. They were very happy with their work. Then, a strong wind came and blew the leaves all around, mixing them up again. The three friends looked at the mixed leaves and laughed. The big bear said, "Even though the wind mixed the leaves, we had fun working together." The small rabbit and the fast deer agreed. They learned that it is important to have fun and work together, even if things don't stay perfect. And so, the three different friends played in the colorful leaves, happy that they had each other. They knew that working together and having fun was the most important thing. And the forest was filled with their laughter and joy.

One day, a big, big dog and a small cat played a game. The game was to see who could dry the most water. The winner would get an enormous toy. The dog and the cat were very excited. The dog said, "I will win! I am big and strong!" The cat said, "I will try my best!" They both started to dry the water. The dog used his big paws and the cat used her small paws. The sun was very hot and helped them dry the water too. But then, something happened. The sun was too hot, and the water dried up too fast. The dog and the cat could not finish the game. They both lost. They were sad and did not get the enormous toy. The moral of the story is to not be too sure of winning and to always be careful when playing games.

One day, a little ball named Bo wanted to bounce high. Bo loved to bounce, but he wanted to see a rainbow. He tried to bounce hard, but he could not reach the sky. Bo met a big ball named Ben. Ben said, "I can help you bounce high. We can do it together." Bo was happy and said, "Thank you, Ben!" The next day, Bo and Ben bounced hard together. They bounced higher and higher. Bo saw the pretty rainbow in the sky. Bo was so happy, he said, "We did it, Ben! I can see the rainbow!" They both smiled and kept bouncing, knowing they could do anything together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his blocks. One day, he wanted to build a big tower with his blocks, but he couldn't find his favorite red block. So, Tim started to search for it. He looked under his bed and asked his teddy bear, "Teddy, have you seen my red block?" Teddy shook his head. Tim kept searching. He looked in the toy box and asked his toy car, "Car, have you seen my red block?" The car shook its head too. Finally, Tim found his red block in a fragile box. He was very careful when he took it out. Tim said, "Thank you, box, for keeping my red block safe!" He built a big tower with his blocks and was very happy.

One day, Ellie was picking flowers from the garden. She was picking dandelions, roses, and daisies. The sun was shining and the sky was blue. Ellie smiled as she saw the night come. She loved night time! The stars shone in the dark sky and there were so many sparkles. Suddenly, she heard someone call out her name. It was her aunt! She had come to visit for the evening. Auntie asked "Ellie, shall we pick a bedtime story for tonight?". Ellie nodded excitedly. Auntie chose a kind story about a family that was always happy and never argued. Ellie liked the story and fell asleep quickly after. She had a good night's sleep and woke up feeling refreshed the next morning.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. Today, she wanted to play outside, but the wind was harsh. She put on her coat and hat to stay warm. Sarah saw a big box outside. She wanted to open it. Inside, she found a pretty kite. Sarah was very happy and wanted to play with the kite. She held the kite and ran with it. The wind lifted the kite high in the sky. Sarah laughed and played until the sun went down. It was a fun day for her.

Once upon a time, there was a big, colorful crane. The crane had many friends in the forest. One day, the crane met a little bird who was sad. "Why are you sad?" asked the crane. The little bird said, "I want to build a nest, but I don't know how." The crane thought for a moment and said, "I recommend you ask the wise old owl. He knows many things and can help you." The little bird thanked the colorful crane and went to find the wise old owl. The owl taught the little bird how to build a strong nest. The little bird was very happy and thanked the owl. From that day on, the little bird and the colorful crane became best friends. They played together and helped other animals in the forest. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a mole named Momo lived in a big garden. Momo was a reliable mole who always helped his friends. He liked to dig tunnels in the dirt and play with his friends. One day, Momo met a big bird named Benny. Benny was sad because he lost his favorite toy. Momo wanted to help him, but Benny said, "No, I don't permit you to help me. You're too small." Momo felt sad, but he didn't give up. He asked his friend, the ant, to help him find Benny's toy. They looked and looked, and finally found it under a big rock. Momo and the ant worked together to move the rock and get the toy. Momo brought the toy back to Benny and said, "Look, I found your toy!" Benny was very happy and said, "Thank you, Momo. I'm sorry I didn't permit you to help me before. You are a reliable friend." From that day on, Momo and Benny were best friends. They played together in the garden and had lots of fun. And Benny always knew he could count on Momo to help him when he needed it.

One day, a funny dog named Spot went to the mall. He wanted to find a new toy to play with. Spot was very happy to be at the mall. Spot started to search for the toy store. He looked left and right, but he could not find it. He asked a nice lady for help. She said, "The toy store is over there." Spot wagged his tail and said, "Thank you!" Spot found the toy store and went inside. There were so many toys! He picked a big, bouncy ball to play with. Spot was very happy with his new toy. He left the mall and went home to play with his ball. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Joy and a tired old man named Dave. One day, Joy saw the old man walking down the street and decided to tease him. She ran up beside him, poked him in the arm and said, "Hi Dave! You look tired!" Dave said, "Yes, indeed I am! I've been helping my neighbor fix his tire for hours!" Joy smiled and said, "Well, let me help you. I'm really good at changing tires!" Dave was surprised, but pleased. He soon realized she was right and together, the two of them changed the tire in no time! When they were finished, Joy said, "See how much faster we were with two people working on the tire? That was so much fun!" Dave smiled and said, "Yes, it sure was. I'm glad you helped me today, Joy. You made it a jolly good time!" Joy beamed with joy and they both smiled all the way back home.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mandy who was very attractive. One day, Mandy was sitting on her porch eating her favorite food - pizza. Out of nowhere, Tommy, the neighbor's 3 year old son, came up to her. Tommy smiled up at Mandy, “Hi, Mandy. Can I have a bite?” Mandy smiled back, “Sure! Sit here and have a slice.” Tommy eagerly sat next to Mandy and grabbed a slice of pizza. He said, “This pizza is yummy!” Mandy nodded in agreement. “Yes, it's yummy. We can eat it together.” The two of them sat there and enjoyed the pizza until it was all gone. Mandy gave Tommy a big hug and he went home, happy.

Sara loved to go to the zoo with her mom. She liked to see all the different animals and learn their names. Her favorite animal was the rhinoceros. She thought it was big and strong and had a funny horn on its nose. One day, Sara and her mom went to the zoo and saw a sign that said "Rhinoceros Feeding Time". Sara was very excited and wanted to see the rhinoceros eat. She asked her mom if they could go closer to the fence. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful and not touch the fence. Sara and her mom walked to the fence and saw a big rhinoceros eating some hay. Sara was amazed by how big its mouth was and how loud it chewed. She wanted to say hello to the rhinoceros and make friends with it. She leaned over the fence and waved her hand. She said "Hi, rhinoceros! You are very nice. Can I pet you?" The rhinoceros heard Sara's voice and looked up. It saw Sara's hand and thought it was food. It opened its mouth and moved its head towards Sara. Sara did not know what the rhinoceros wanted. She thought it wanted to play with her. She smiled and moved her hand closer. Her mom saw what was happening and got very worried. She knew the rhinoceros could hurt Sara with its teeth or horn. She shouted "Sara, no! Don't touch the rhinoceros! It might bite you!" She grabbed Sara's arm and pulled her back from the fence. Sara was surprised and scared. She did not understand why her mom was angry and why the rhinoceros was not friendly. She started to cry and said "Mom, why did you do that? I just wanted to pet the rhinoceros. It looked so nice." Her mom hugged Sara and said "I'm sorry, Sara. I know you like the rhinoceros, but it is not a pet. It is a wild animal. It does not know you and it might think you are food. You have to be careful around wild animals. They can be dangerous. I love you and I don't want you to get hurt." Sara calmed down and said "I love you too, mom. I'm sorry I made you worried. I didn't know the rhinoceros was wild. Can we still watch it eat?" Her mom said "Yes, we can. But we have to stay away from the fence and not touch it. OK?" Sara said "OK, mom. Thank you for letting me see the rhinoceros. It is still my favorite animal. But I will not try to pet it again." Her mom said "You're welcome, Sara. I'm glad you like the rhinoceros. But remember, some animals are better to look at than to touch."

One day, a little girl named Sue got a new hat. She was very happy. She wanted to tell her friend Tom about her new hat. Sue ran to Tom's house to show him. When Sue got to Tom's house, she saw Tom had a new hat too! Sue said, "Look, Tom! I have a new hat!" Tom said, "I have a new hat too, Sue!" They both laughed and were very happy. Then, a big wind came and blew their new hats away. Sue and Tom were sad. But, they saw a big tree with many hats on it. They found their new hats and more! Sue and Tom took their hats and gave the other hats to their friends. Now, everyone had a new hat and they all played together.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to eat carrots. One day, Remy found an unusual carrot. This carrot was very big and had a funny shape. Remy was very happy and excited to eat this big carrot. Remy started to eat the unusual carrot. But, Remy was very tired from playing all day. So, Remy decided to rest for a little while before eating more of the carrot. Remy lay down under a tree and closed his eyes. While Remy was resting, something unexpected happened. The unusual carrot began to move! It was not just a carrot, but a friendly caterpillar who looked like a carrot. The caterpillar said, "Hello, Remy!" Remy was very surprised but happy to have a new friend. From that day on, Remy and the caterpillar played together and shared many carrots.

Once upon a time, in a big, big forest, there was a mighty ant. The ant was very strong and loved to walk on a trail. One day, while walking, the ant met a tiny bug. "Hello, tiny bug," said the mighty ant. "Do you want to walk on the trail with me?" The tiny bug looked up and answered, "Yes, I would like that." So, the mighty ant and the tiny bug walked on the trail together. They talked and laughed as they walked. They were having so much fun. But then, something unexpected happened! The tiny bug grew bigger and bigger until it was even bigger than the mighty ant! The ant was very surprised. "Wow, you are not a tiny bug anymore!" said the mighty ant. "Now, we can both be strong and walk on the trail together." And so, the mighty ant and the big bug became best friends. They walked on the trail every day, helping each other and having fun.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Jack. He was feeling very lonely. He was walking around in the woods looking for someone to talk to. "Is anyone here?" he asked. Suddenly, he heard a loud sneeze. He looked around and he saw a rabbit. Jack was very happy to find a friend. "Hi rabbit! What are you doing here," he asked. The rabbit replied. "I'm going on a march right now. Would you like to come with me?" Jack was very excited and said he would join. So the two of them started their march together. They sang songs and laughed and had an amazing time. But then suddenly, Jack sneezed... and he kept sneezing! His nose was dripping and he could not stop. The rabbit said that he had to go back home, and so he left. Jack was left alone. He realised that he must have gotten a cold. He wished he had stayed at home, in the warmth and comfort of his own home. He learned that it is important to take care of yourself and stay warm.

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent dog named Max. Max lived in a small house with his best friend, a little girl named Lucy. One day, they wanted to go to the park, but it was raining. Lucy had an idea. She took her umbrella and said, "Max, let's go!" At the park, they saw a big tree with a cat stuck in it. The cat was wet and scared. Max wanted to help the cat. He had an idea. He held the umbrella in his mouth and started to climb the tree. It was hard, but Max did not give up. He wanted to succeed. Max reached the cat and opened the umbrella. The rain stopped falling on the cat. The cat was happy and climbed onto the umbrella. Then, something unexpected happened. The umbrella started to float like a magic carpet! Max, the cat, and the umbrella floated down to the ground. Lucy was so surprised! They all became friends and went home together. From that day on, Max and the cat shared the magic umbrella whenever it rained.

Once upon a time, in a big tree, there was a raven. The raven liked to perform tricks for his friends. He would fly high, then low, and do flips in the air. All the other birds would watch and clap their wings. One day, the raven saw a shiny thing on the ground. He picked it up with his beak and took it to his nest. But the shiny thing belonged to a little girl. She was sad and looked for it everywhere. The raven felt guilty for taking the shiny thing. He wanted to make the little girl happy again. So, the raven took the shiny thing back to where he found it. The little girl saw it and was very happy. The raven performed a happy dance in the sky for her, and they both became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a silly cat named Tim. Tim loved to play with a big ball of metal. One day, Tim saw a big dog that wanted to play with him. But Tim was scared of the big dog, so he ran away and hid. Tim hid behind a tree and watched the big dog. The big dog found the metal ball and started to play with it. Tim wanted his metal ball back, but he was still scared. He thought, "If I quit being scared, I can get my metal ball back." So, Tim took a deep breath and walked up to the big dog. The dog looked at Tim and wagged its tail. Tim realized the big dog just wanted to be friends. They played with the metal ball together and had lots of fun. From that day on, Tim and the big dog were best friends, and Tim never felt scared again.

One day, a girl named Sally went to the store with her mom. They took a big cart to put things in. Sally liked to push the cart with her mom. They went down many rows to find what they needed. Sally saw a thick book on a shelf. She wanted the book, but she could not reach it. Sally's mom helped her get the book. Sally was very happy. She put the book in the cart. At the end, they went to pay for the things in the cart. Sally realized she forgot to get a toy. She was sad, but her mom said they could come back another day. Sally felt better and went home with her mom.

Lily liked to play basketball with her big brother Tom. Tom was very good at basketball. He could throw the ball very high and make it go in the hoop. Lily wanted to be good like Tom, but she was still small and could not throw the ball very high. One day, Tom said he would teach Lily how to play better. He said the first thing she needed to learn was how to speed. Speed means to run very fast with the ball. Tom showed Lily how to speed. He ran very fast with the ball and passed by Lily. Lily tried to catch him, but he was too fast. Lily said, "Tom, you are too fast for me. How can I speed like you?" Tom said, "You have to practice, Lily. You have to run every day and make your legs strong. And you have to be modest. Modest means to not think you are better than others. If you are modest, you will work hard and learn from your mistakes." Lily nodded. She wanted to be modest and learn from Tom. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother and a good teacher. I will practice and speed like you." Tom smiled. He said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a good sister and a good student. I am proud of you." They hugged and played some more basketball. Lily tried to speed and throw the ball high. Sometimes she missed, but sometimes she made it. Tom cheered for her and helped her. They had fun and learned a lot.

Billy was a little boy who wanted to ride his bike. He was very excited and got his helmet on. His mum told him to be careful and he promised he would be. He rode his bike around the block. Then, he blinked and suddenly there was a truck! Billy was so scared and he skidded off the road into a mud puddle. His helmet was covered in mud and he was very miserable. Billy's mum rushed over to him and hugged him tight. She wiped the mud off his helmet and looked into his eyes. Suddenly, Billy started to laugh. His mum smiled. She was so happy that he was okay. Billy finished his ride and when he got back home he hugged his mum again. He had learned a lesson and promised that he would be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there was a big farm. On the farm, many vegetables grew. There were thick carrots, round tomatoes, and green peas. The farmer loved his vegetables and took good care of them. One day, a little girl named Sally came to visit the farm. She saw the farmer with a long stick. The farmer was using the stick to measure the vegetables. Sally asked, "What are you doing?" The farmer said, "I am measuring my vegetables to see how big they have grown. Would you like to help me?" Sally was happy to help. She took the stick and measured the thick carrots. They were very big! Together, they measured all the vegetables on the farm. Sally had a fun day at the farm. She learned how to measure and found out how big the vegetables can grow. The farmer thanked Sally for her help and gave her some vegetables to take home. Sally couldn't wait to come back to the farm and help again.

One day, a cat and a dog were in the kitchen. They wanted to prepare a good snack. The cat said, "We have bread and jam. Let's make a sandwich!" The dog agreed, "Yes, that sounds yummy!" They looked for the bread and found it on the left side of the kitchen. The cat jumped up and grabbed the bread. The dog got the jam. They worked together to make the sandwich. They were very happy. But then, something unexpected happened. A little mouse came out from under the fridge. The mouse said, "Can I have some too?" The cat and the dog were surprised but they said, "Sure, we can all share!" So they all sat down and enjoyed their good sandwich together.

One day, Mommy and Daddy decided to go on a trip to the city. They told their three year old daughter, Hope, to stay at home and make sure she was safe. Hope wanted to be a brave girl, so she promised to stay inside and play by herself. After her parents left, Hope went upstairs to her room. She wanted to be a big girl and explore, so she decided to open the closet door. When she opened the door, she was greeted with a dangerous sight: a big, white snake was in the closet. Hope was so scared that she jumped back in fright. She tried calling for help, but she couldn't find the right words. Out of the blue, Hope's cat Leo came to the rescue. Leo hissed at the snake and chased it out of the closet. Hope was so relieved and thankful to her brave cat. Hope and Leo then managed to close the closet door. From that day forward, Hope promised to be careful and never open the closet without an adult around. Mommy and Daddy were so proud when they heard what Hope managed to do.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a tall oak tree. A little cat lived near the oak tree. The cat liked to play and stretch near the tree every day. The cat was happy. One day, the cat saw a big bird on the oak tree. The cat wanted to play with the bird, but the bird was too high. The cat tried to stretch and jump, but it could not reach the bird. The cat felt frustrated. The cat tried again and again to jump and stretch, but it still could not reach the bird. The bird saw the cat and flew away. The cat was sad and went back home. The cat never saw the bird again.

One day, a big bus went down the road. It was a sunny day, and the bus was full of happy kids. They were going to the pool to swim and play. At the pool, the kids put on their swim clothes. They jumped in the water and swam like fish. They laughed and splashed each other. It was so much fun! One little boy splashed too much water on a girl. She was sad and wet. The little boy felt sorry. He said, "I am sorry" to the girl. She smiled and said, "It's okay!" They swam together and had a great day at the pool.

Once there was a little girl called Lily. One evening, she was playing outside when the stars started to glow. She was so happy that she couldn't help but smile. Lily had a bag in her hand and she reached inside. It was full of sparkly things that glowed in the night. She threw them into the air and they flew all around, twinkling and sparkling in the moonlight. The sparkles kept flying and Lily kept playing until her mom called her in. Inside her house, mama said it was time for bed. But then something special happened. When Lily looked out the window, she could see a big loud light outside! She ran outside and there was a rainbow glowing in the sky. It was so bright and big that Lily just couldn't believe it. The colors kept changing and they were even brighter than the stars! Lily savored every moment until finally, the sky grew dark again and the rainbow faded away. But Lily went to bed with a smile on her face, knowing that the amazing rainbow would come back some day.

Once upon a time, there was a fast bunny named Bob. Bob lived in a small home underground. He liked to play outside and get dirty. One day, Bob's mom said, "Bob, you must clean your room today." Bob did not like to clean, but he wanted to make his mom happy. So, he started to clean his underground room. While cleaning, Bob found a toy car he had lost. He was so happy! He showed his mom the toy car and said, "Look, Mom! I found my car!" His mom smiled and said, "Good job, Bob! Now your room is clean and you have your car back." Bob learned that cleaning can be fun and helpful. From that day on, he always kept his underground home clean and tidy. And he and his mom lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a light dog with a big heart. He loved to play with his friends, run around, and bark at the birds in the sky. Spot seemed like a very happy dog. One day, Spot's friend, a small cat named Whiskers, got sick. Whiskers had to go to the doctor for an operation. Spot was sad and worried about his friend. After the operation, Whiskers came back home. Spot was very happy to see his friend again. But something was different. Whiskers seemed bigger and stronger now! The operation had made Whiskers grow. Now, Spot and Whiskers could play even more fun games together.

One day, a big van came to the park. A bossy man got out of the van. He had a lot of toys. He said, "I will give toys to the kids who play with me." A girl named Sally saw the man and said, "I want to play with you!" The bossy man said, "You must do what I say." Sally did not like that, but she wanted the toys. So she played with the bossy man. After a while, Sally did not have fun. She did not like being bossed around. She decided to stop playing with the bossy man. Sally said, "I don't want your toys. I want to play with my friends." The bossy man was sad, but Sally was happy playing with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing with her toys in her room when her mom came in. Her mom seemed upset. Lily asked, "Mom, what's wrong?" Her mom said, "I just got some bad news. Our dog, Spot, is lost. He ran away from the yard." Lily felt sad because she loved Spot. Lily and her mom went outside to look for Spot. They called his name and walked around the neighborhood. They asked their friends if they had seen Spot, but no one had seen him. It was getting dark, and they had to go home. Lily was very upset and cried. The next day, Lily and her mom put up signs with Spot's picture. They hoped someone would find him and bring him home. But after many days, Spot did not come back. Lily learned that it's important to always keep the gate closed so that pets don't get lost.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Max and Zoe. Zoe was a brave kid with a big heart. One day, she wanted to go for a zoom with Max. But Max was afraid of heights. Max said he didn't want to go. Zoe tried to convince him, but he wouldn't listen. Zoe wanted to help Max face his fear, so she took out her open umbrella. She asked Max to get on and hold the handle, then she said she would make it rise up high in the sky. At first, Max was very scared. His heart was beating fast. But he held the handle, and soon the umbrella rose up, higher and higher. Max looked outside and it felt like they were flying! He could finally take in all the views around. He realised that he hadn't needed to be scared all along, and was so happy to have his zoom with Zoe. They laughed and talked all the way, staying in the sky all day long!

One day, a bright sun was shining in the sky. A big cloud was floating by. A little girl named Lily was playing outside. She saw the cloud and had an idea. Lily ran to her mom and said, "Mom, can we attach a string to the cloud and pull it down?" Her mom smiled and said, "We can try, but it might be hard to reach." Lily and her mom found a long string. They tied a rock to the end of the string. They threw the rock up to the cloud, but it did not attach. They tried again and again, but the rock always fell down. Just then, a bird flew by and saw them trying. The bird said, "I can help you attach the string to the cloud!" The bird took the string in its beak and flew up to the cloud. It attached the string to the cloud. Lily and her mom pulled the string, but the cloud did not come down. Instead, the cloud pulled them up into the sky! They were surprised and laughed as they floated with the cloud. The bird flew with them, and they all had a fun day in the sky.

One day, a bright sun was up in the sky. Tim and Sue went outside to play. They wanted to build a big sandcastle. They took their toys and started to build. As they built, they felt hot and thirsty. Sue said, "Let's drink some juice!" Tim agreed and they went inside to get juice. They found apple juice and orange juice. Tim liked apple juice, and Sue liked orange juice. They drank their juice and felt better. They went back outside to finish their sandcastle. It was big and pretty. Tim and Sue were happy with what they built. They played until the sun went down. Then, they went inside to eat dinner and sleep. They had a fun day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lily. She was excited because spring was here. The sun was up, the flowers were out, and the birds were singing. Lily loved spring because she could play outside with her friends. One day, Lily went to the park with her friend, Tim. They saw a big tree with pretty flowers. "Look, Tim!" said Lily. "The tree is so pretty!" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, it is! Spring is the best!" Lily and Tim played under the tree all day. They laughed and had fun. They knew that spring was a special time. And they were very happy to be together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to paint. He would paint all day long. One day, Tim found a big brick. The brick was not like other bricks. It was black. Tim thought the black brick was special. He wanted to paint something on it. So, he got his paint and brush. Tim painted a big, happy face on the black brick. The face was yellow and had a big smile. Tim showed his painted black brick to his mom. She loved it! She put the brick in the garden. Now, every time Tim looked at the black brick, he would smile. And the painted happy face on the brick smiled back at him.

One day, a little ant named Tim was walking in the grass. He saw a big piece of cake. Tim was very hungry and thought, "I want that cake all for me." He did not want to share with his ant friends. Tim was being selfish. As Tim tried to take the cake, he heard a voice. It was a big bird named Bob. Bob said, "Do you want help with the cake?" Tim was scared but said, "Yes, please help me." He thought maybe he should not be so selfish. Bob picked up the cake with his beak. He flew high in the sky with the cake and Tim. Then, something unexpected happened. Bob dropped the cake! It fell down and broke into many pieces. Tim was sad, but he learned that being selfish was not good. He shared the cake pieces with his ant friends, and they all ate happily together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw on paper. One day, she saw her mom hide a big paper in a box. Lily was very curious about what was on the paper. The next day, when her mom was in the kitchen, Lily decided to peek at the paper. She opened the box and saw a scary picture on the paper. Lily got scared and ran away from the box. She did not want to look at the scary picture again. Later, her mom found Lily crying in her room. She asked Lily what was wrong. Lily told her mom about the scary picture on the paper. Her mom smiled and said, "That was just a picture I drew for a silly game." She showed Lily that the scary picture was not real, and they both laughed. From that day on, Lily was not scared of the paper anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very tired. He went to look for a handle to pick himself up. After walking for a while, he saw a handle leaning against a big tree. The boy thought this handle looked just like what he was looking for and so he quickly grabbed it. Suddenly, the handle started to become bigger and bigger. The boy became scared and tried to put the handle down. But it had become too big for him to handle! The boy tried to get away, but the handle kept growing. Pretty soon, the boy became so tired that he couldn't move. He kept trying to get away, but the handle was much too big for him. In the end, the handle grew so big that it squashed the poor boy, and he was never seen again.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a shy little girl named Lily. She had a hard time making friends because she was too scared to talk to other kids. One day, she saw a big dog in the park. The dog looked like a threat to her, and she was very scared. Lily thought she should run away, but then she heard a voice. "Don't be scared, I'm a nice dog," said the dog. Lily was surprised that the dog could talk, but she decided to trust him. They started to play together, and Lily felt happy. As they played, other kids saw them and wanted to join. Lily was shy at first, but the dog helped her talk to the other kids. Soon, Lily made many friends. The moral of the story is: don't judge someone or something by how they look. Sometimes, the things that seem scary can bring us the most joy.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor named Tom. Tom had a big, ugly sack. He took the sack with him everywhere he went. One day, Tom met a little girl named Sue. Sue saw the ugly sack and asked, "What's in the sack, sailor?" Tom smiled and said, "I'll show you, Sue." He opened the sack, and out came a pretty, red ball. Sue was very happy to see the ball. She and Tom played with the ball all day. They had so much fun. When the sun went down, it was time for Sue to go home. "Thank you for playing with me, sailor," said Sue. Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Sue. I'm glad you liked my ugly sack." They both laughed, and Sue went home. From that day on, Tom and Sue were best friends. They played together every day and had lots of fun. And the ugly sack was not so ugly anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot was a very confused dog. He loved to chew on things, but he didn't know what he should chew on. One day, he found a big bottle of oil in the kitchen. Spot thought it would be fun to chew on the bottle. "Spot, no!" said his friend, Cat. "You should not chew on the oil bottle! It is not good for you!" But Spot didn't listen. He chewed and chewed until the bottle broke. The oil went all over the floor. Spot was very surprised and didn't know what to do. Cat came to help Spot clean up the oil. As they worked together, Spot learned that he should listen to his friends when they try to help him. He also learned that some things are not good to chew on. From that day on, Spot only chewed on his toys and never on things that could be bad for him. And Cat and Spot became even better friends.

Once upon a time in a far away land, there lived two friends. One was called Bob and the other was called Sam. Bob was very attractive and was always smiling. Sam was very supportive of Bob and always there to lend a helping hand when needed. One day, Sam invited Bob over for a barbecue. Sam had set up a very attractive grill in his garden. Bob was so excited and they began to cook various delicious treats. As they sat down to eat, Bob said to Sam, "thank you for inviting me over. I really appreciate all your support over the years." Sam smiled and replied, "of course, you can always count on me for support". They enjoyed their barbeque and both went home happy and full.

Benny was a dog who liked to run and play. He had a big yard with a fence and a tree. He had a bowl of food and water that his human gave him every day. He was happy and healthy, except for one thing. He had fleas. Fleas are tiny bugs that bite and itch. They live in Benny's fur and make him scratch and whine. Benny tried to get rid of them by rolling on the grass and shaking his head, but they did not go away. He wished his human would provide him with something to make them stop. One day, a new human came to visit. He had a bag and a smile. He said hello to Benny and petted him. Benny liked the new human. He smelled good and was gentle. The new human took out a bottle from his bag and said, "This is a brilliant flea spray. It will kill all the fleas on your dog and make him feel better. Can I use it on him?" Benny's human nodded and said, "Sure, go ahead. I've been meaning to get something for him, but I've been busy. Thank you for helping him." The new human sprayed the bottle all over Benny's fur. Benny felt a cold and wet sensation. He did not like it. He tried to run away, but the new human held him. He said, "Don't worry, it will be over soon. It's for your own good." Benny started to feel funny. He felt dizzy and weak. He could not breathe. He looked at his human with scared eyes. He wanted to say, "Help me, something is wrong." But he could not make a sound. He fell to the ground and did not move. The new human looked at Benny and said, "Oops, I guess I used the wrong bottle. This is not flea spray, this is poison. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hurt him. I mixed them up." Benny's human screamed and cried. He ran to Benny and hugged him. He said, "No, no, no, this can't be happening. Benny, please wake up. Please don't die. You're my best friend. I love you." But Benny did not wake up. He did not hear his human. He did not feel anything. He was gone. The fleas were gone too. But so was Benny. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted little frog named Freddy. Freddy lived near a big river. He had many friends who liked to play with him. One day, Freddy saw a pretty flower on the other side of the river. He thought it would be a nice gift for his mom. Freddy told his friends about the flower. They all wanted to help him get it. They knew Freddy was very good at jumping. So, they kneeled down by the river and made a plan. Freddy would jump from one friend's back to the next friend's back, all the way across the river. The next day, Freddy and his friends got ready. They kneeled by the river and started the plan. Freddy jumped from one friend to the next, all the way across the river. At last, he reached the pretty flower and picked it. Freddy jumped back across the river with the flower. He gave the pretty flower to his mom. She was so happy and proud of her gifted little frog. Freddy and his friends had a big party to celebrate their success. From that day on, they knew they could do anything if they worked together.

Once upon a time, there lived a young girl called Sally. She lived in a village near the sea. One day, Sally decided to go for a walk along the shore. As she walked past the water, she noticed how icy it felt beneath her feet. Sally shivered and put her hands in her pockets. Suddenly, she felt something hard against her finger. She reached in and found a round, smooth pebble. She smiled and picked it up. Just then, Sally heard a loud noise. It sounded like something had been struck in the water nearby. She looked around and saw a small fish leaping out of the sea. The fish had been struck by a large wave and was hurt. Sally was sad and wanted to help. She remembered the stone in her hand and slowly threw it in the water. Suddenly, the pain and suffering of the small fish faded away. Sally smiled and realised the power of kindness. She learned that everyone can make a difference, no matter how small.

Once upon a time, there was a new robot. The robot was big and shiny. It could talk and play with kids. One day, the robot met a little boy named Tim. Tim said, "Hi, robot! Can you lend me your toy car?" The robot was happy to help. It gave Tim the toy car to play with. They played together all day long. At the end of the day, Tim gave the toy car back to the robot. They both said "bye" to each other. Tim went home and the robot went to find more friends to play with. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little girl named Sue found a big hoop in her yard. She loved to play with the hoop. She would roll it, spin it, and jump through it. Sue was very happy with her hoop. One sunny day, Sue saw a big pot outside. She had an idea. She took her hoop and used it to stir the pot. As she stirred, the pot began to shake. Sue was surprised! She did not know what was happening. Suddenly, the pot turned into a big, tough bear! The bear looked at Sue and said, "Thank you for stirring the pot. I was stuck inside, and now I am free!" Sue and the bear became friends, and they played with the hoop together.

Once upon a time, in a big green garden, there lived a wise caterpillar named Catty. Catty was very smart and loved to help her friends. One day, while she was crawling on a leaf, she saw a little bird crying. "Little bird, why are you crying?" Catty asked. "I can't find my mommy," the little bird said, tears in his eyes. "Can you help me, please?" Catty knew just what to do. She told the little bird to grab onto her back, and they started to look for his mommy together. They crawled and hopped around the garden, asking all the animals they met if they had seen the little bird's mommy. Finally, they found her near a big tree, looking very worried. The little bird was so happy to see his mommy again. He hugged her tight and thanked Catty for her help. From that day on, Catty and the little bird became best friends, and they played together in the big green garden every day. And everyone in the garden knew that wise caterpillar Catty was always there to help her friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy, who was walking in the park. As he walked he could hear the birds singing in the trees. Suddenly, he heard a loud voice say, "Hello!" He stopped and looked around. He saw a big table with lots of food on it. He started walking towards it and soon he could smell something warm and delicious. He realised it was lunchtime, and he was very hungry. He looked at the table, and he saw it was full of hot food. He quickly started eating the hot food, it was so yummy! After he had finished his lunch he felt happy and very full. He thanked the voice he had heard earlier and said goodbye as he continued his adventure.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. He saw his friend, the lazy cat, lying under a tree. The cat was sleepy and did not want to play. Tim wanted to find something fun to do, so he looked up at the sky. He saw a big, bright star up in the sky. Tim thought it was the most beautiful star he had ever seen. He wanted to touch the star, but it was too high up. So, he got a big stick and tried to reach it. Tim swung the stick up to the sky to touch the star. But he was too short, and the stick was not long enough. He felt sad, but then he had an idea. He ran inside and got a cloth. He came back out and wiped the stick with the cloth. It was now a magic stick! Tim reached up to the sky again, and this time, he could touch the star. The star was happy to be friends with Tim and the lazy cat. They all played together and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a clean aeroplane. It was very big and shiny. It liked to fly high in the sky. The aeroplane had many friends who were also aeroplanes. They all liked to play together. One day, the clean aeroplane wanted to fly higher than it ever had before. But it was a little scared. Its friends saw that it was scared and wanted to help. They said, "You can do it! We will encourage you!" The clean aeroplane felt happy to have such good friends. With the help of its friends' encouragement, the clean aeroplane flew higher and higher. It was so happy to be in the sky. The clean aeroplane looked down and saw all of its friends cheering. The clean aeroplane knew it could do anything with the help of its friends.

Once there was a little bunny, who lived in a meadow near an oasis. But the bunny was very thirsty and wanted something to drink. He was hopping around in the meadow, looking for some water. Suddenly, he saw a light coming from afar. "Maybe that light will show me to some water!", the bunny thought. He ran towards the light, hopping and jumping as fast as he could. The light got bigger and brighter, and the bunny realised that he had reached the oasis. But the squirrels had seen him too, and they were angry. They started jumping around, trying to keep the bunny away. The bunny was so scared that he started to shake, but he was determined. He kept hopping and jumping, until he reached the oasis. He quickly drank as much water as he could and then ran away. He vowed never to forget the oasis and the light that had shown him the way there.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was very friendly and liked playing with his friends. One day, he went outside to the park and saw a shadow on the ground. He was very curious and walked closer to it. When he got close, he noticed a bird was in the shadow. The bird was scared and couldn't fly away. Jack knew it was stuck and he wanted to help. He found a soft towel, put it around the bird, and carefully released the bird back into the sky. The bird was so happy that Jack had helped it. It circled Jack's head a few times and then flew away, creating another friendly shadow. Jack smiled and went back home, feeling proud that he had helped the bird.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big nose. He was always ready to play with his friends. One day, Tim and his friends went to the park. They played on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. Tim's friend, Sam, wanted to tell a funny story. He told a story about a dog with a very long nose. The dog's nose was so long that it could touch the ground. Tim and his friends laughed and laughed. They thought the story was very funny. After playing all day, Tim and his friends were tired. They said goodbye and went home. Tim was happy that he had a big nose, just like the dog in the story. He was always ready to tell the funny story to his friends and make them laugh.

Once upon a time, there were twin boys named Tim and Jim. They were very close and loved to play together. One day, they saw a high tree in their yard. They wanted to climb it and become brave. Tim and Jim started to climb the high tree. They went up, up, up. They were having so much fun. They could see their house and yard from the top. They smiled and laughed as they climbed higher. When they reached the top, they felt very brave. They had become good climbers. Tim and Jim were happy twins. They climbed down the high tree and ran to tell their mom and dad about their big adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. Joe was three years old and loved to go to the park to play. One day, Joe was walking through the park when he noticed something blue in the sand. He picked it up and discovered it was a teaspoon. He asked his Mum what it was, and she said it was a teaspoon for feeding. Joe was very excited. His mum opened a small box from her bag and gave Joe some food for the teaspoon. Joe liked to feed the birds and was very happy. He walked to the park bench and put the food in the spoon. Then he stood back and waited. Soon, the birds came and started to feed from the teaspoon. Joe stared in amazement. He had never seen such beautiful blue feathers on birds before. Then, Joe began to smile. He was so happy, he wanted to feed the birds again and again.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little dog named Tim. Tim loved to play with his purple ball. One day, while he was playing in the park, he saw a big tree. Tim wanted to see what was up in the tree, so he got close and sniffed. "Help! Save me!" cried a little bird from the tree. Tim looked up and saw the bird stuck in a nest. The bird was scared and could not fly. Tim wanted to help the bird, so he thought of a plan. Tim ran to his purple ball and pushed it near the tree. He climbed on the ball and jumped high. He grabbed the bird with his mouth and jumped down. "Thank you for saving me!" said the little bird. Tim was happy he could help, and they both played with the purple ball all day.

Sara likes to play with her dolls. She has many dolls, but her favorite is Lily. Lily has long hair and a pink dress. Sara likes to brush Lily's hair and give her massages. She thinks Lily is very patient and nice. One day, Sara's mom says they have to go to the store. Sara wants to bring Lily, but mom says no. She says Lily might get lost or dirty. Sara is sad, but she listens to mom. She puts Lily on her bed and says goodbye. She tells Lily she will be back soon. At the store, Sara sees many things. She sees toys, books, candy, and clothes. She wants to look at everything, but mom says they have to hurry. Sara notices a big sign that says "Sale". She wonders what it means. Mom takes Sara to a section with many dolls. Sara sees dolls that look like Lily, but they are not Lily. They have different dresses and faces. Sara thinks they are not as pretty as Lily. She misses Lily. She asks mom if they can go home. Mom says yes, but first she has to buy something. She picks up a doll that looks like Lily, but has a blue dress. She says it is for Sara's cousin, who has a birthday soon. Sara thinks her cousin will like the doll, but she wishes mom would buy her something too. Mom pays for the doll and they leave the store. Sara is happy to go home and see Lily. She hopes Lily is not lonely or angry. She thinks Lily will be happy to see her. But when they get home, Sara has a big shock. She runs to her room and looks for Lily. But Lily is not on her bed. Lily is gone. Sara sees a note on her pillow. It says "Sorry, Sara. I sold Lily to a lady who gave me a lot of money. She said she liked Lily's massages. Love, Dad." Sara is very sad and angry. She cries and screams. She does not understand why dad would do that. She does not care about money. She only cares about Lily. She wants Lily back. She hates dad. She hates the lady. She hates everyone. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty skirt that she loved to wear. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. The park was very noisy because there were many kids playing and laughing. While playing, Lily saw a big dog. The dog ran to her and jumped on her. Lily's pretty skirt got dirty from the dog's paws. She was very sad and began to weep. She didn't know what to do. Lily's friends saw her crying and came to help. They took her to a nearby water tap and helped her clean her skirt. After the skirt was clean again, Lily stopped weeping. She thanked her friends and they all went back to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim was a troubled boy. He did not like the dark. Every night, when it was time to sleep, Tim would cry. He was scared of the dark. One day, Tim's mom had an idea. She said, "Tim, let's write a letter to the dark. We will tell the dark that you are scared." Tim liked this idea. He said, "Okay, mom. Let's write the letter." Tim and his mom wrote the letter. They said, "Dear dark, please do not scare Tim. He is a good boy." They put the letter under Tim's bed. That night, Tim was not scared. He slept well. The dark was now his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a mischievous seal named George. Every day, George liked to play pranks on his neighbors and cause trouble! One day, he decided to spray orange paint on the homes of his friends and family. "George, why did you spray orange paint on everyone's houses?" asked his mother. George giggled and said, "I just wanted to have fun!" His mother looked very unhappy. "George, you have to stop this bad behavior!" his mom warned. But George was stubborn and he continued to spray paint on the homes of everyone he knew. His friends and family got very angry and decided to hatch a plan to stop him. They decided to capture George and convince him to stop his mischievous behavior. One day, they finally managed to catch George and showed him how his misbehavior had affected others. George felt really sad about what he had done and he vowed never to spray orange paint again. He apologized to everyone and from that day on, he was a good seal and was no longer causing trouble in the neighborhood.

One day, a boy named Tim went on a trip with his mom and dad. They went to a big park with lots of trees and flowers. Tim was very happy because he loved to play outside. While Tim was playing, he felt cold. He realized he did not have his warm coat. He ran to his mom and dad and told them he was cold. They gave him a big, warm hug and his coat to wear. Now, Tim was not cold anymore. He played all day with his mom and dad at the park. They had a fun trip and went home when the sun went down.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they found a big, old book under a tree. It had many pictures and words inside. "Look, Ben, this book is ancient!" Lily said. "It is very old and dusty. Maybe it has magic stories!" Ben opened the book and saw a picture of a dragon. He pointed at it and said, "Wow, Lily, this is a dragon! It can fly and breathe fire. I wish I could see a real dragon!" Lily smiled and said, "Maybe we can, Ben. Maybe this book can take us to the dragon's land. Let's read it and find out!" They sat down under the tree and started to read the book. They enjoyed the stories of knights, princesses, and wizards. They imagined they were in the book, having adventures and fun. They did not notice the time passing by. Soon, the sun was setting and their moms came to pick them up. They hugged each other and said goodbye. "Did you have a good time, Lily?" her mom asked. "Yes, mom, I had a lot of success!" Lily said. "I found an ancient book with Ben and we read about dragons!" "That sounds wonderful, Lily. I'm glad you enjoyed your day. But now it's time to go home and have dinner. You can bring the book with you and read more tomorrow." Lily nodded and put the book in her backpack. She waved at Ben and his mom and got in the car. She was happy and excited. She could not wait to read more of the ancient book and see more dragons.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat delicious food. His favorite food was cake. One day, Tim saw a big cake in the kitchen. It had lots of weight. He was very happy. Tim wanted to eat the whole cake by himself. He did not want to share it with his friends. So, he hid the cake under his bed. Every day, he would eat a little bit of the cake. It was so delicious. But one day, Tim started to feel sick. His tummy hurt a lot. He ate too much cake. He did not share the cake with his friends. Now, Tim was sad and sick. The delicious cake was not good for him.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big sack. They put toys and snacks in the sack. They carry the sack together. One day, they see a wide slide. It is shiny and red. They want to go on the slide. They leave the sack under a tree. They run to the slide. They take turns to slide down. They laugh and have fun. But then, a mean boy comes. He sees the sack. He wants to take it. He sneaks to the tree. He grabs the sack. He runs away. Lila and Ben see the mean boy. They are sad and angry. They shout at the mean boy. "Hey, that is our sack! Give it back!" Lila says. "No, it is mine now! Finders keepers!" the mean boy says. Lila and Ben chase the mean boy. They are fast and strong. They catch the mean boy. They take the sack from him. They scold the mean boy. "That is not nice! You are a thief! You should share and be kind!" Ben says. The mean boy is scared and sorry. He says sorry to Lila and Ben. He gives them a toy car. He asks them to be his friends. Lila and Ben are reliable friends. They forgive the mean boy. They share their toys and snacks with him. They invite him to play on the slide. They all become friends. They have a happy day.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tim. He lived in a small house with a garage. Tim loved to play in the garage with his toys. One day, Tim heard a noise in the garage. He was scared but wanted to know what it was. Tim went inside the garage and saw a big box. The box was shaking! Tim asked, "Who is in the box?" The box did not answer. Then, the box opened, and a little kitten jumped out! Tim was so happy and surprised. He thought the noise was from something big and scary, but it was just a cute, little kitten. They became best friends and played in the garage every day.

Lily liked to study books with pictures and words. She wanted to learn many things. She had a neighbor named Tom who also liked to study books. They sometimes studied together and shared their books. One day, Lily found a big book with many pictures and words. It was about animals and plants and places. She was very happy and wanted to show it to Tom. She ran to his house and knocked on the door. "Tom, Tom, look what I have!" she said, holding the book. Tom opened the door and saw the book. He was impressed by the book. He wanted to see it and study it. "Wow, Lily, that is a very impressive book. Can I see it?" he asked. "Sure, Tom, we can study it together. Come on, let's go to my house," Lily said. They went to Lily's house and sat on the floor. They opened the book and looked at the pictures and words. They saw lions and elephants and giraffes. They saw mountains and rivers and forests. They saw many things they did not know. They were so busy studying the book that they did not hear Lily's mom calling them for lunch. They did not hear Lily's dad coming home from work. They did not hear Lily's dog barking. They only heard a loud noise when Lily's dad stepped on the book by accident. He did not see the book on the floor. He was angry and shouted. "What is this? Who left this book here? This is a very expensive book. It belongs to my boss. He lent it to me for a project. How could you be so careless?" Lily and Tom were scared and sad. They did not know the book was not Lily's. They did not know the book was very expensive. They did not know the book belonged to Lily's dad's boss. They only wanted to study the book and learn. They tried to say sorry, but Lily's dad did not listen. He took the book and threw it in the trash. He told Lily and Tom to go away and never touch his things again. Lily and Tom ran away crying. They felt bad and ashamed. They lost the book and their friend. They did not want to study books anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little farm. On this farm, there were many animals. There were cows, pigs, and chickens. They all lived happily together on the farm. One day, a new animal came to the farm. The other animals did not recognize it. So, they asked, "Who are you?" The new animal said, "I am a sheep. My name is Fluffy." The other animals were happy to meet Fluffy. They played together all day on the little farm. They became very good friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a drive. It was a cold day, so they wore warm coats. Tim's mom gave him a napkin and said, "Keep this with you, it may help later." As they drove, they saw a big tree with a cat on top. The cat was scared and could not come down. Tim had an idea. He took the napkin his mom gave him and tied it to a long stick. He said to the cat, "Hold on to this napkin, and we will pull you down." The cat held on to the napkin, and Tim and Spot pulled the stick. The cat came down, but it was not a cat! It was a small tiger! The tiger was happy to be down and said, "Thank you, Tim and Spot. I was lost and scared. You helped me, and now I can go home." Tim and Spot were surprised but happy they could help. They all became friends and went for more drives together. And Tim always remembered to bring a napkin, just in case.

There were two children, Peter and John. Peter was 3 years old and John was 5 years old. They were playing in the park one day when Peter saw something shiny in the grass. He went to take a closer look and saw it was a stone. He picked it up and showed it to John. John said it was a magic stone. He said if they whispered something to the stone it could make their wishes come true. Peter was so excited. He closed his eyes and whispered his wish to the stone. John said the stone needed a powerful pitch to make it work. Peter tried again and this time he made sure to whisper loudly. He opened his eyes and saw something had changed. Peter was scared and asked John what was going on. John said, "It's too late. We can't take it back." The powerful pitch of Peter's whisper had created a giant monster that had destroyed the park! The two children ran away as fast as they could.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Tim. Tim loved to crawl on the ground and play with his friends. One day, Tim found a big spoon in the grass. He thought it was a fun toy to play with. Tim showed the spoon to his friend, Sally the snail. Sally said, "Wow, that's a tight fit for me to crawl on!" Tim and Sally took turns crawling on the spoon and sliding down it like a slide. Later, Tim and Sally met their friend, Billy the bee. Billy saw the spoon and asked, "What's that?" Tim replied, "It's a spoon, and it's fun to crawl on!" All three friends played with the spoon until it was time to go home. They had a great day playing together with their new toy.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Max. Max loved to play and help his family. One day, Max saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was sad because she could not find her bowl. Max said, "Don't worry, I will help you find your bowl." They looked around the house but they could not find it. Max and Lily started to struggle. They looked under the bed and behind the couch. Still, they could not find the bowl. Finally, Max found the bowl in the kitchen. "Here it is!" Max said. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Max! You are a very good and dependable friend." Max wagged his tail and they played together all day.

One day, Orin was walking through the dark forest. He saw a herb and decided he wanted to pick it. He did not dare to pick the herb because he was scared of the dark. Then he heard a voice, it said, "You can do it Orin, you can pick the herb". Orin was surprised and he asked, "Who's there?". Out of the shadows stepped a little rabbit. He said, "I'm a magical rabbit. I'm here to help you". Orin was amazed and quickly picked the herb. The rabbit said, "Well done Orin". Then he said, "I have one more task for you. I dare you to focus all your courage and go into the darkest part of the forest". Orin was scared but he was also excited. He clenched his fists and marched forth into the darkest part of the forest. After a while, Orin returned and the little rabbit said, "I knew you could do it". In that moment, brave Orin realized that he can do anything he sets his mind to.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl called Sue. She was 3 years old and loved playing outside. One day Sue was looking around her garden. She saw something new and exciting. It was a tall jar full of goodies! She ran over to have a look. Sue wanted to take a closer look so she pointed at the jar and said, “What is this?” Her mom smiled. “That’s a jar full of lollipops!” she said. Sue was excited but soon realised the jar had a lid on it that was too tough for her to open. She looked sadly at her mom. “Don’t worry, Sue,” said her mom. “Let’s get a spoon and try to open the jar together.” Sue smiled and got a spoon from the kitchen. Together she and her mom opened the jar and Sue was able to get her lollipop!

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to make things with sticks, stones and leaves. They were very creative. Sara made a house for her doll. Tom made a car for his toy bear. But then, a big wind came and blew their things away. Sara and Tom were sad. They cried and hugged each other. "Look, Sara, your doll is hurt!" Tom said. He saw a cut on the doll's arm. "We need to help her." "How?" Sara asked. "We need a bandage. Come, I know where to find one." Tom said. He took Sara's hand and ran to the shed. In the shed, they found some old cloth and scissors. Tom cut a piece of cloth and wrapped it around the doll's arm. He tied a knot and smiled. "There, your doll is better now. The bandage will make her heal." Tom said. "Thank you, Tom. You are very kind." Sara said. She hugged Tom and the doll. They went back to the garden. They saw their sticks, stones and leaves scattered on the ground. "Let's restore our things. We can make them again." Sara said. "OK, let's do it. We can make them even better." Tom said. They worked together and made a new house and a new car. They were happy and proud. The moral of the story is: Be kind and helpful to your friends. Don't give up when things go wrong. Use your creativity to solve problems.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bird. The bird lived in a big tree. The bird had many friends. One day, a girl saw the pink bird. The girl wanted to give the bird a gift. She found a pretty box. The girl put the gift in the box. The girl went to the tree. She called the pink bird. The bird came down. The girl gave the box to the bird. The bird opened the box. It was a cat! The cat jumped out and chased the pink bird. The bird tried to fly away, but the cat was too fast. The pink bird was not seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Lily. She loved to sort her toys and draw pictures. One day, she drew a big picture of her toys and showed it to her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "Lily, you are so good at sorting and drawing. One day, you will help others with your skills." As Lily grew up, she kept sorting and drawing. One day, she found a box full of mixed up toys. She thought, "I will sort these toys and make other kids happy too." Lily worked hard and sorted all the toys into neat piles. She drew a picture of the sorted toys and put it on the box. Soon, a sad boy named Tom found the box of sorted toys. He saw the picture and smiled. He played with the toys and became happy. Tom shared the toys with other kids, and they all became happy too. Lily's mom was right – her sorting and drawing skills made others happy. And so, Lily learned that helping others and sharing her skills could bring happiness to everyone. She kept sorting and drawing, making more kids happy each day. The unexpected twist was that Lily's simple skills could make such a big difference in the world. The moral value of this story is to always share your talents and help others, as it can bring happiness to everyone.

Once upon a time there was a lovely little girl called Ruby. She was playing in the park one day and when she looked up she saw a big, furry rabbit on a bench. She was so excited that she ran to it and tried to give it a big, cuddly hug. But the furry rabbit didn't like it and it bit her on the arm. Ruby was so scared that she started to cry. Just then, a kind old man came over and told Ruby that the rabbit had only bitten her because it was feeling frightened. He told her that animals are just like humans and that sometimes it's better to be kind and understanding towards them, rather than trying to hug them all the time. Ruby was thankful for the old man's words and she was so grateful that he'd shown her kindness. From then on, whenever she went to the park, she made sure to be gentle and understanding towards all the animals and they were all very happy. The moral of this story is that it's important to be gracious and respectful of all creatures, no matter how small. When we show love and kindness towards animals, everyone is much happier.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray bird. The bird lived in a big tree. The bird liked to sing and play all day. One day, the bird found a rock. The rock was small and smooth. The bird picked up the rock with its hand. The bird wanted to play with the rock. The bird and the rock played together. They rocked back and forth on the tree branch. They had so much fun. The bird and the rock were very happy. And they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little dolphin named Dolly. She lived in the big blue sea. Dolly was sad because she was all alone. She wanted to find a friend to play with. One day, Dolly saw a big group of dolphins swimming together. She swam up to them and said, "Hi, I am Dolly. Can I play with you?" The other dolphins looked at her and said, "No, you are too small and poor. You cannot play with us." This made Dolly very sad. Dolly swam away and found a nice turtle named Timmy. Timmy saw that Dolly was sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Dolly?" Dolly told Timmy about the other dolphins who did not want to play with her. Timmy said, "Don't worry, Dolly. We can be friends and play together." So, Dolly and Timmy played together and had lots of fun. They knew that being poor or small did not matter. They were happy to be friends and not separate.

Once upon a time there was a painter in a far away land. He had been painting pictures for many years, but he was clumsy. One day, he had to go away and he decided to pack some things. As he was packing his belongings, he dropped his favourite brush. "Oh no," he said, in a sad voice. Just then, a little boy appeared. He was only three years old. “What's wrong?” the little boy asked the painter. “I dropped my brush,” the painter replied. The little boy smiled, and said "I can help! I'm really good at packing things!" So, the painter and the little boy finished packing together. The painter thanked the little boy for his help, and they said goodbye. The painter went on his way, filled with happiness. Even if he was clumsy, he had made a friend!

One day, Mummy and Daddy drove to the farm to buy some beef. When they arrived, Daddy said, “We are so lucky! Look at all the cows!”. Mummy smiled and said, “Yes, and I’m sure one of these cows will give us some yummy beef.” Suddenly, a big dog appeared, barking loudly. Mummy was scared, and she shouted, “Oh no! Get in the car quickly.” Daddy drove fast, but the dog followed after them. Mummy was worried and said, “We need to get away from that dog or it won’t be so lucky for us!” In the end, Daddy drove very fast and the dog didn’t follow them anymore. Mummy said, “Let’s go back and get some beef for our dinner now that the dog has gone.” They drove back to the farm, and this time the dog was nowhere to be seen. Mummy was so happy and said, “We were so lucky! We were able to get the beef after all!” Daddy smiled and nodded in agreement, and they drove home with their yummy beef.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the kitchen. He saw his mom standing next to the freezer. Tim felt sleepy and let out a big yawn. "Mom, I am tired," he said. His mom looked at him and smiled. "Why don't you go play outside, Tim?" she said. "It will help you wake up." Tim nodded and went outside to play. While playing, Tim found a filthy toy car in the dirt. He picked it up and said, "Ew, this car is dirty!" He ran inside to show his mom. "Look, mom! I found a dirty car outside!" he said. His mom took the car and cleaned it for Tim. Now he had a clean toy car to play with, and he was not sleepy anymore.

There was a modern town where people liked to help each other. In this town, there was a beautiful stream. The water in the stream was clean and shiny. All the people and animals loved the stream. One day, a little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went to the stream to play. They saw a big fish in the water. The fish said, "Hello, Tim and Spot! Can you provide me with some food? I am very hungry." Tim and Spot wanted to help the fish, so they looked for food near the stream. While they were looking, something unexpected happened. They found a magic stone near the stream. The stone said, "If you give me to the fish, he will become a friend who can talk and play with you." Tim and Spot were very excited. They gave the magic stone to the fish. The fish ate the magic stone and turned into a big, friendly fish that could talk and play with Tim and Spot. They all became best friends and had lots of fun together. And from that day on, the stream became even more special to the people in the modern town.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to read books. Every day, he would go to his bookshelf and grab a book. He was eager to learn new things from the books. One day, Tim saw a big, red ball outside his window. He wanted to play with it. He put the book back on the bookshelf and ran outside. He grabbed the ball and played with it all day long. When the sun went down, Tim went back inside his house. He was eager to read another book. He grabbed a book from the bookshelf and sat down. Tim read the book and learned about a big, blue sea. He was happy to read and play every day.

Once upon a time, in a gloomy town, there lived a little boy named Tim. He loved to eat lollipops. One day, he saw a big lollipop in a shop. He wanted it very much but had no money. Tim had an idea. He took a sack and went to his friend, Sam. Tim said, "Let's fill this sack with toys and sell them. Then we can buy the big lollipop." Sam liked the idea and they filled the sack with toys. They went to the market but nobody wanted to buy their toys. The sky turned dark and it started to rain. Tim and Sam were sad. They took the sack and went home. They never got the big lollipop.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived an elderly bear. He was big, brown, and very kind. All the little animals liked him a lot. They would play and laugh with him all day long. The elderly bear would tell them stories and teach them new things. One sunny day, the elderly bear mentioned a big party he wanted to have. He said, "Let's have a fun party with all our friends!" The little animals were very happy and excited. They clapped their hands and jumped up and down. So, they all helped to plan the big party. They picked pretty flowers, made yummy food, and played happy songs. All the animals in the forest came to the party. They danced, ate, and had a great time. The elderly bear smiled and laughed with them. It was the best party they ever had.

Once upon a time, there was a big, generous hippo. He lived in a pond with many friends. The hippo liked to help his friends and share his food with them. One day, the hippo's friend, a little bird, came to him. The bird was sad. "I want to build a nest, but I need more sticks," said the bird. The generous hippo wanted to help his friend. He thought, "I can add sticks to the bird's nest." The hippo went to find sticks near the pond. He picked up the sticks with his mouth and carried them to the bird. The bird was so happy. "Thank you, hippo," said the bird. "You are a good friend." Together, they added more sticks to the nest. The bird's nest became big and strong. All the friends in the pond were happy. They knew they could count on the generous hippo to help them when they needed it. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to watch cool movies. One day, he saw a new movie about a big blue bear. The bear could talk and play games. Tim thought the bear was very cool. Tim's friend, Sue, came over to play. Tim said, "Sue, let's watch a cool movie. It has a big blue bear." Sue was happy and said, "Yes, I want to see the bear!" They sat down to watch the movie together. While they watched the movie, the big blue bear told them to stay and play with him. Tim and Sue stayed and played games with the bear. They had so much fun. When the movie ended, they said goodbye to the bear. Tim and Sue smiled and knew they found a new cool friend in the movie.
