Once upon a time, there was a poor judge who lived in a small house. He was a kind man who always helped others. He had a garden where he wanted to grow big and tasty vegetables. One day, he planted a seed in his garden. He watered it and gave it lots of love. The seed started to grow. It grew into a tall and strong plant with beautiful green leaves. As the plant grew, the poor judge became very happy. He knew that soon he would have tasty vegetables to eat and share with his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big building with an elevator. The elevator went up and down, taking people to different floors. One day, a little boy named Tim went inside the elevator with his mom. Tim was very light and small. As the elevator went up, Tim started to jump. His mom said, "Tim, please stop jumping in the elevator." But Tim did not listen. He kept jumping, and the elevator stopped working. Tim and his mom were stuck inside. A kind man named Sam heard them call for help. He knew how to save them. Sam pressed a button on the outside of the elevator, and it started working again. The elevator door opened, and Tim and his mom were free. Tim said, "Thank you, Sam!" From that day on, Tim never jumped in the elevator again.

Once upon a time, there was a little baby who loved to crawl. He would crawl all around the house on his knees. One day, he saw an open door. He thought, "I want to see what is behind that door!" So, he crawled and crawled until he got to the open door. As the baby crawled through the open door, he saw a big, soft ball. The baby was so happy! He knew that he had found something fun to play with. He crawled closer and closer to the big, soft ball. He could not wait to touch it and play with it. The baby finally reached the big, soft ball. He played with it all day long. He was so glad that he had crawled through the open door. The baby knew that if he kept crawling and exploring, he would find even more fun things to do.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big box. It was closed. Lily was very patient and waited for her mom to come see the box. "Mom, can we open the box?" she asked. Her mom said, "Yes, let's open it." When they opened the box, they found a book of memories. It had pictures of Lily when she was a baby. "Look, mom! It's me!" said Lily. They both laughed and looked at the pictures together. They were so happy. But then, something unexpected happened. A little boy came running to them. "That's my memory book!" he said. Lily and her mom looked at each other. They realized that the book was not theirs. The little boy was very nice and let them keep one picture. Lily learned that it is important to be patient and always make sure something belongs to you before taking it.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl named Lily. One day, Lily got an invitation to a fun party at her friend's house. She was very happy and excited to go. Lily wanted to look pretty for the party, so she tried to match her dress with her shoes. She found a blue dress and blue shoes that looked nice together. She put them on and felt like a princess. At the party, Lily and her friends played games, ate yummy snacks, and danced to fun music. They all had a great time. When the party was over, Lily said "thank you" to her friend for the fun time and went home with a big smile on her face.

Once there was a child named Jim. Jim was three years old and he was very curious. He used to look up at the sky and admire the distant clouds. One day, while looking up at the sky, Jim saw a balloon. He wanted to touch it. He ran and jumped and he was determined to reach it. Jim asked his mom, "Mommy, can I lift the balloon?". Mommy said, "Maybe if the weather is nice". The sky was sunny and clear, so Mommy said yes. Jim stretched out his arm and he lifted the balloon. Jim was so happy. He smiled and laughed. He said to the balloon, "Let's fly high". The balloon flew away into the distant sky. Jim waved goodbye to the balloon and he knew he would never forget this moment.

One day, there was a famous man named Jack. He liked to jog every morning. He went outside and put on his special socks. The socks were made especially for running. They were very soft, and he felt comfy in them. Jack started to jog around the park. He ran past a lake, a tree and a big, green hill. He jogged around and around for a long time. He felt happy and truly enjoyed his morning jog. When he was finished jogging, Jack started to wave to the people around him. Some clapped and cheered, because he was famous! Jack smiled and felt very proud. The next morning, Jack put on his special jogging socks and started to jog around the park again. He didn't feel tired at all and it felt really good to stretch his legs. He jogged around and around, smiling with joy as he waved to the people around him.

Once upon a time, there was a blue star named Sparkle. Sparkle lived up in the sky with her friends, the other stars. They all liked to play together at night. One day, a new star came to the sky. His name was Twinkle. Twinkle was shy and didn't know how to make friends. Sparkle saw Twinkle and wanted to help him. Sparkle went up to Twinkle and said, "Hi, I'm Sparkle. Welcome to the sky! Do you want to play with us?" Twinkle smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to play with you!" So Sparkle and Twinkle played with the other stars all night long. They had so much fun, and Twinkle was very happy. From that day on, Twinkle and Sparkle were best friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big book with many pictures. They want to see the pictures, but the book is too heavy. They try to pull the book, but it does not move. "Let me help you," says a voice. It is Mr. Lee, the librarian. He is kind and smart. He lifts the book and puts it on a table. "This is a special book," he says. "It has stories and secrets. Do you want to hear one?" "Yes, please!" Lily and Ben say. They sit on the floor and listen to Mr. Lee. He opens the book and shows them a page. It has a picture of a dragon and a knight. "This is a story about a brave knight and a friendly dragon," he says. "They have a big adventure together." Lily and Ben are curious. They want to know more. They lean closer to the book and look at the picture. They see something shiny in the corner. It is a sticker. It has a star and a smiley face. Lily likes stickers. She reaches for the sticker and tries to peel it off. "Wait, Lily, don't do that!" Ben says. He knows that stickers are not for taking. They are for keeping. He grabs Lily's hand and stops her. But it is too late. Lily has torn the page. She has made a big hole in the picture. She has ruined the book. Lily and Ben are scared. They look at Mr. Lee. He is not happy. He is sad and angry. He sees the torn page and the sticker. He shakes his head and sighs. "Oh, Lily, why did you do that?" he says. "This is a very old and precious book. You can't tear it. You have to be careful and gentle. You have to respect the book and the stories." Lily feels bad. She knows she has done something wrong. She is sorry. She wants to fix the book. She wants to make Mr. Lee happy. She looks at him with big eyes and says, "I'm sorry, Mr. Lee. I didn't mean to tear the book. I like the book. I like the stories. I like the sticker. Can I give it back to you? Can I glue the page? Can I say sorry to the book?" Mr. Lee sees Lily's eyes and hears her words. He is still sad and angry, but he is also kind and smart. He knows that Lily is a good girl. He knows that she is young and curious. He knows that she has learned a lesson. He smiles and winks at her. He says, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You can give me the sticker. You can help me glue the page. You can say sorry to the book. And you can still hear the story. Do you want to hear the story?" "Yes, please!" Lily and Ben say. They hug Mr. Lee and say thank you. They say sorry to the book and touch the page. They sit on the floor and listen to Mr. Lee. He tells them the story of the brave knight and the friendly dragon. He shows them the pictures and the secrets. He makes them laugh and wonder. He makes them happy. He is kind and smart. He is their friend.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a very tall tree. The tree was very gentle and kind to all the small animals that lived in the forest. One sunny day, a little bird named Timmy wanted to find a new home. Timmy saw the gentle tree and thought, "This tree looks like a nice place to live." He flew closer to the tree and said, "Hello, gentle tree. May I enter and live in your branches?" The gentle tree smiled and said, "Of course, little bird. You are welcome to enter and make a home here." Timmy was very happy. He entered the tree and made a cozy nest in its branches. He lived there with his family, and they all became good friends with the gentle tree. They all lived happily ever after in the big forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. She liked to have fun and explore the world around her. One day, Sophie decided to explore her mommy's kitchen. As Sophie looked around, she saw an interesting looking machine on the counter. It was so exciting and she wanted to find out what it was. She asked her mommy, "What is this?" Mommy smiled and said, "That's a coffee machine! It makes coffee for adults. Do you want to try it?" Sophie nodded eagerly and gave it a squeeze. But it wasn't very comfortable and it made her feel a bit uncomfortable. Her mommy laughed and said, "Oh Sophie, I think it's best if adults use the coffee machine." Sophie smiled and went back to exploring the kitchen. She was glad her mommy was there to help her and make her feel better.

Tim and Lily are playing with their crayons and paper. They like to draw different things, like animals, cars, and flowers. Tim draws a big lion with a yellow crayon. Lily draws a pink car with a purple crayon. "Look at my lion!" Tim says. "He is very strong and loud. He can scare anyone." "Look at my car!" Lily says. "It is very fast and pretty. It can go anywhere." They show each other their drawings and smile. They are proud of their work. But then, Tim sees something on Lily's paper. It is a small mark with a green crayon. It looks like a bug. "Hey, what is that?" Tim asks. He points at the mark. "That is nothing," Lily says. She tries to hide the mark with her hand. "It is just a mistake." "A mistake?" Tim says. He grabs Lily's paper and looks closer. "It is a bug! You drew a bug on your car!" Lily feels angry and embarrassed. She did not mean to draw a bug. She was trying to draw a flower, but the green crayon slipped from her hand. "It is not a bug!" Lily says. She tries to get her paper back. "It is a flower!" Tim does not believe her. He thinks she is lying. He laughs at her. "A flower? That is a silly flower. It has no petals, no stem, no leaves. It is just a dot. A green dot. A bug!" Lily feels more angry and sad. She does not like Tim laughing at her. She wants to erase the mark. She looks around and sees an eraser on the table. It is a big, white eraser. It is flexible and soft. She has an idea. She reaches for the eraser and pushes Tim away. She rubs the eraser on her paper, hard and fast. She wants to make the mark disappear. "Stop it!" Tim says. He pushes Lily back. He wants to keep the paper. He thinks it is funny. "You can't erase a bug! It is still there!" They push and pull, push and pull. They fight over the paper and the eraser. They do not hear their teacher coming. "Tim! Lily! What are you doing?" their teacher says. She is not happy. She sees the paper and the eraser. She sees the crayons and the drawings. She sees the mark and the mess. She takes the paper and the eraser from them. She looks at them with a stern face. "You two need to calm down and apologize," she says. "You need to respect each other's work and feelings. You need to share and be nice." Tim and Lily feel ashamed and sorry. They know they did wrong. They look at each other and say sorry. "I'm sorry, Lily," Tim says. "I should not have laughed at your drawing. It is not a bug. It is a flower." "I'm sorry, Tim," Lily says. "I should not have pushed you and erased your drawing. It is not a mistake. It is a lion." They hug and make up. They give each other their paper and their crayon. They finish their drawings and add more details. They make the lion more fierce and the car more shiny. They make the flower more colorful and the bug more friendly. They show their teacher their drawings and smile. They are proud of their work and their friendship.

One day, a girl named Lily went to her grandma's house. She saw a big armchair. It was a rare chair. Lily liked the chair a lot. She sat on it and felt very happy. Lily's mom said they had to leave soon. Lily did not want to go. She liked the armchair too much. She wanted to stay with the chair all day. But Lily's mom said they had to go. Lily was sad. She gave the armchair a big hug. She said bye to the rare chair. She knew she could come back and see it again.

One day, a girl named Sue found a flute. Sue liked the flute. She wanted to play it. Sue was a generous girl. She liked to share her toys with her friends. Sue went to her friend Tom's house. She wanted to play the flute with him. But when Sue got to Tom's house, she slipped on a toy. The flute flew into the air. The flute landed in a tree. Sue and Tom were sad. They wanted to play the flute. But then, a bird flew down from the tree. The bird had the flute in its beak. The bird gave the flute to Sue. Sue and Tom were happy. They played the flute together. The bird sang along with them. It was a fun day for all.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore the kitchen. One day, she saw a green thing on the table that looked like a ball. She picked it up and felt its smooth skin. She wondered what was inside. She asked her mom, "What is this, mom?" Her mom smiled and said, "That is an avocado, Lily. It is a fruit that you can eat. But you have to cut it open first." Lily wanted to see what was inside the avocado. She looked for something to cut it with. She saw a knife on the counter. She reached for it, but her mom stopped her. "No, no, Lily. You can't use the knife. It is sharp and dangerous. You can hurt yourself. Give it to me, please." Lily was not happy. She wanted to cut the avocado herself. She did not want to give the knife to her mom. She held it tight and said, "No, mom. I want to cut it. I want to see." Her mom was worried and firm. She said, "Lily, you have to listen to me. The knife is not a toy. You can rub the avocado with your hands, but you can't cut it. Give me the knife, now." Lily did not want to listen. She tried to pull the knife away from her mom. But her mom was stronger and took the knife from her. Lily started to cry. She felt angry and sad. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I know you are curious, but you have to be careful. The knife can hurt you and make you bleed. I don't want you to get hurt. I love you." Lily calmed down and said, "I love you too, mom. But I still want to see the avocado." Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, Lily. I will show you the avocado. But you have to promise me to never touch the knife again, okay?" Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I promise." Her mom cut the avocado in half and showed Lily the soft flesh and the big seed inside. Lily was amazed. She rubbed the avocado with her fingers and tasted it. She liked it. She said, "Mmm, the avocado is yummy. Thank you, mom." Her mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it. But remember, be careful and listen to me, okay?" Lily said, "Okay, mom. I will."

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy loved the color purple. One day, she found a purple object in her room. It was a pretty purple box with a shiny button on it. Amy was very curious about the box. Amy showed the purple box to her friend, Tom. Tom said, "Don't push the button, Amy. We don't know what it does." But Amy didn't listen. She pushed the button and a loud noise came out of the box. It scared them both and they started to cry. Amy's mom heard the noise and came running to see what happened. She saw the purple box and asked, "Did you push the button, Amy?" Amy said, "Yes, Mommy. I'm sorry. I regret pushing the button." Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay. We all make mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them and listen to our friends when they try to help us." From that day on, Amy learned to be more careful and listen to her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was a poor girl who lived in a small house with her mom. Lily loved to eat yogurt. One day, her mom bought her a big cup of yogurt. Lily was very happy. Lily sat down to eat her yogurt. She was so excited that she spilled some yogurt on the floor. "Oh no!" said Lily. Her mom came into the room and saw the mess. "Lily, you need to clean the floor," said her mom. Lily got a cloth and started to clean the yogurt from the floor. She worked hard to make the floor clean again. When she was done, her mom smiled and said, "Good job, Lily! Now you can finish your yogurt." Lily was happy that she could help her mom and eat her yogurt too.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Max. Max loved to play with his boy, Tim. They had lots of fun together. They played with a ball, they ran in the park, and they went for long walks. One day, Max and Tim saw a ladder near a big tree. Tim wanted to climb the ladder, but Max was scared. Tim said, "Don't worry, Max. I will be safe." So, Tim climbed up the ladder, but when he got to the top, he was too scared to come down. Max knew he had to help his friend. He tried to climb the ladder, but he couldn't do it. Max was sad, but he did not give up. He ran to Tim's mom and barked loudly. Tim's mom followed Max and saw Tim stuck in the tree. She helped Tim get down from the ladder. The moral of the story is that we should always be loyal and help our friends, even when we are scared. Sometimes, the unexpected can happen, but if we work together, we can face any challenge.

One day, a lovely little cat named Kitty went outside to play. She saw her friend, Doggy, who was playing with a ball. Kitty wanted to join Doggy, so they played together all day long. They had so much fun in the sun. As they played, Kitty's mom called her inside. "Kitty, come and drink your milk!" she said. Kitty ran inside and drank her milk. She knew it was important to listen to her mom. Doggy waited outside, wagging his tail. After Kitty drank her milk, she felt strong and happy. She went back outside to play with Doggy. They played and played until the sun went down. Now, Kitty understood why her mom wanted her to drink her milk. It made her strong, so she could play with her friend all day long. And that made Kitty very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big scary spider. It lived in a small house with a little girl named Lily. Lily did not like the spider. She thought it was too scary. But the spider insisted it was nice. One day, Lily saw the spider in her room. She was scared and wanted it to go away. But the spider insisted it wanted to show her something. Lily was curious, so she decided to see what the spider wanted to show her. The spider took Lily to a secret place in the house. There, she saw a big box. Lily opened the box, and inside she found a lot of toys! It turned out the spider was not scary at all. It just wanted to share the toys with Lily. From that day on, Lily and the spider became best friends.

Once, there was a helpful girl named Sue. She liked to help her mom with the house work. One day, her mom asked her to fold her new blouse. Sue was happy to help. Sue took the blouse to her room. She tried to fold it, but it was hard. She tried again and again. She started to feel sad. She thought, "I need to find a way to fold this blouse right." Then, Sue had an idea. She went to her big sister's room. She asked her sister to show her how to fold the blouse. Her sister was kind and showed her how to do it. Sue watched and learned. Sue went back to her room and tried to fold the blouse again. This time, she did it right! She was so happy that she could help her mom. Sue learned that it's okay to ask for help when you need it.

Once upon a time, in a big red stable, there lived a kind horse named Henny. Henny had many friends that lived with her in the stable. They played games and ate yummy hay together. One day, Henny's leg started to hurt. She couldn't play with her friends and felt sad. Henny's best friend, a little boy named Timmy, saw that she was hurt. He wanted to help her feel better. Timmy went to his dad and asked for help. His dad knew what to do. He got a key to unlock a special room in the stable. Inside the room, there was a soft, warm bed for Henny to rest her hurt leg. Timmy and his dad helped Henny to the bed. She felt much better and thanked Timmy for his help. After a few days, Henny's leg didn't hurt anymore. She could play with her friends again and they all lived happily in the big red stable.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a girl named Sally. Sally had a light, pretty kite. Tim wanted to play with the kite too. So, they made a trade. Tim gave Sally his toy car and Sally let Tim play with her kite. "Wow, this kite is so fun!" said Tim. "I love our trade," said Sally. They played all day and were very happy. But then, a big wind came and took the kite far away. Tim and Sally were sad. They had to delay their play time to look for the kite. They walked and walked until they found the kite stuck in a tree. Tim and Sally worked together to get the kite out of the tree. When they got the kite back, they were very happy again. They learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but they can still have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was an old tree in the forest. One day, a young bear wanted to climb the old tree. She asked the kind owl sitting on the branch, "Can I climb the old tree?" The kind owl said, "Yes! Just be careful!" The young bear slowly, carefully started to climb. She tried to grab onto all the old branches as she made her way up. Once at the top of the tree she let out a cheer! She looked around and saw all the old, gnarled branches. She was happy to be safe and high up in the old tree. Suddenly, she heard a voice say, "Hey! That was a very good climb!" She looked around and noticed the kind owl looking at her. The young bear smiled and thanked the kind owl for his help in her climb. She waved goodbye and made her way down the old tree. The young bear continued to climb many old trees in the forest and have lots of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a big, fast cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with a long cord. He would run and jump, trying to catch the cord. Tom's friend, Sam, would hold the other end of the cord and move it around for Tom to chase. One day, Sam had an idea. He wanted to print a picture of Tom playing with the cord. Sam had a small camera that could print pictures. He asked Tom to play with the cord, and Tom was very excited. Sam moved the cord fast, and Tom chased it. Tom jumped high and caught the cord in his paws. Sam took a picture with his camera and printed it. Tom and Sam looked at the picture together. They both smiled, happy to have a memory of their fun day playing with the cord.

Once upon a time there was a little princess who owned a very special pet - it was a King bird. The Princess liked to take her pet bird for long walks around the kingdom. One day the princess asked the King bird to fly faster, but the King bird disagreed and started to complain. The Princess, who was very wise, noticed the bird’s dissatisfaction. “Why are you complaining?” asked the Princess. The King bird replied,“I can’t fly as fast as other birds, and I don’t like it.” The Princess smiled and said, “You don’t have to be the fastest bird in the world to be special. Each of us have our own unique gifts and talents, and that is what makes us special.” The King bird was happy and set off again, this time not complaining, but feeling proud of his unique abilities. The moral of the story is that comparison doesn’t always lead to happiness, and that we should all be proud of who we are and what we can do.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a fat dog with a shiny collar. The dog was chewing on something. Ben and Lily wanted to see what it was. "Hello, doggy. What are you chewing?" Ben asked. He tried to pet the dog, but the dog growled and moved away. "Maybe he is chewing a bone. Dogs like bones," Lily said. She followed the dog, but the dog ran faster. The dog stopped near a fountain. He dropped what he was chewing. It was not a bone. It was a coin. A big, gold coin. "Wow, look at that! A coin!" Ben said. He ran to pick it up, but the dog barked and snapped at him. "Bad dog! That is not your coin. That is for people," Lily said. She threw a stick to distract the dog. The dog chased the stick. Ben grabbed the coin and showed it to Lily. "This is a pretty coin. Maybe we can buy some candy with it," he said. Lily nodded. "Yes, let's go to the store. But we have to be careful. The dog might come back and want his coin," she said. They ran to the store, holding the coin tightly. They did not see the dog following them. They did not see the man who was looking for his coin. They did not see the trouble they were in.

John had a delicate math book. He liked to look through its bright pages and practice his sums. One day, he was so eager to practice that he dropped the book on the floor. John slowly crawled on his stomach over to pick it up. He held the book in his hands with the utmost care, to make sure he didn't damage it. Suddenly, John's mother called from the living room, "John! Come here." John scrambled to his feet and put the book safely aside. "Yes mum?" he asked, still crouching on the ground. "John, what have I said about being careful with things?" his mother said, "The book is delicate, remember - it needs special care." John nodded and promised to be more careful. He went back to the book and carefully lifted it, making sure to keep it balanced. Then he crawled into the living room and handed the book to his mother. Smiling, she thanked him and handed it back. From then on, John always took special care when he read and practiced his math. He had learned an important lesson and was glad that he hadn't damaged his delicate book.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to draw with her crayons. One day, she drew a big, pretty picture for her grandma. She wanted to mail it to her. Lucy asked her mom, "Can we mail my picture to grandma?" Her mom said, "Yes, let's go to the mailbox." On the way, Lucy saw a naughty dog. The dog tried to take her crayon. "No, doggy! That's mine!" said Lucy. Lucy and her mom put the picture in the mailbox. The naughty dog watched them, but he didn't take the crayon again. Grandma got the picture and loved it. She called Lucy and said, "Thank you for the pretty picture!" Lucy was very happy.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a little ant. The ant loved to swing. Every day, the ant would go to the park and swing with an enthusiastic smile. The ant was always happy and liked to play with the other bugs. One day, while the ant was swinging, a big wind came. The wind blew the ant off the swing and far away from the park. The ant was sad and scared. The ant wanted to go back to the park and swing, but didn't know how to get there. The ant asked a nice bee for help. The bee said, "If you help me find my flower, I will help you find your park." The ant agreed and they worked together. They found the flower and the park, and the ant could swing again. The other bugs were happy to see the ant back. The moral of the story is that by helping others, we can also help ourselves.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim was an honest boy who always told the truth. One day, Tim saw a big smile on his mom's face. She gave him a small pill to make him feel better. Tim did not like the pill. It was big and hard to swallow. Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. They played with toys and had lots of fun. But then, Tim started to feel sick. He knew he needed the pill to feel better, but he did not want to take it. Sam saw Tim's face turn red and knew something was wrong. Sam told Tim, "You need to take the pill to feel better." Tim thought about it and knew Sam was right. He took the pill and soon felt better. Tim was happy he had an honest friend like Sam who helped him. They continued to play and smile all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a lucky pig. This pig was very special. He could talk to people. One day, the pig went for a walk. He met a little girl. The little girl was lost. The pig asked her a question. "Why are you sad?" The little girl said, "I can't find my mom." The pig wanted to help her. They looked for her mom together. Then, something unexpected happened. The pig found a magic hat. He put it on his head. The pig could now find anyone. He found the little girl's mom. The girl was happy. The lucky pig was a hero.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He loved to play and have fun. One day, Tom went with his mom and dad to a big restaurant. He was very excited. In the restaurant, Tom's mom gave him a menu to look at. Tom wanted to pick what to eat. But he was so excited that he started to tear the menu. His mom and dad were not happy. Tom's mom told him that he was being a spoiled boy. Tom felt sad and said sorry. His mom and dad forgave him. They all enjoyed their food and had a great time. Tom learned to be more careful and not tear things.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally. Sally was playing in the playground when she heard something loud coming from the park. Sally ran over to the park and saw two police officers shouting. They were shouting at a man and the man shouted back at them. Sally was so scared she started to cry out loud. The police heard her and one of them said in a gentle voice, "It's okay Sally, don't be scared, we're just talking". Sally looked up at them, still feeling a bit scared but she felt brave and shouted back, "Okay". The police officers gave her a big smile and went back to talking in their normal voices. Sally was relieved and went back to playing.

Once upon a time, there was a lively rabbit. He lived in a small hole in the ground. He loved to hop and play in the grass. One day, the rabbit saw a big tree. He wanted to stand on the tree and see the world. So, he hopped and hopped to get on the tree. But, he could not do it. Then, a bird came and said, "I can help you stand on the tree." The rabbit was very happy. The bird took the rabbit up to the tree. But, the bird did not let the rabbit stand on the tree. Instead, the bird took the rabbit far away to a place the rabbit did not know. The rabbit was sad and could not find his way back home.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play games. One day, they see a big rat in the park. The rat has long teeth and a long tail. It looks scary. "Let's play a game," Tom says. "Who can get closer to the rat? The one who gets closer wins." Sam is afraid of the rat. He does not want to play. He says, "No, Tom. That is a bad game. The rat can bite us. We should stay away." But Tom does not listen. He wants to win. He says, "Don't be a baby, Sam. I will go first. Watch me." Tom walks slowly to the rat. The rat sees Tom. It makes a loud noise. It runs to Tom. It jumps on Tom. It bites Tom on the arm. Tom screams. He falls to the ground. He cries. Sam runs to Tom. He tries to help him. He says, "Tom, are you okay? I told you it was a bad game. We should have stayed safe." But Tom does not answer. He is hurt. He is bleeding. He is not okay. He does not win. He loses.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat named Tom. Tom lived with a family. The family loved Tom very much. They played with him every day. Tom was very happy. One day, the family went out for a walk. Tom wanted to go too, but he was too small. The family said, "Tom, you stay home." Tom was sad. He watched the family go away. Tom walked around the house. He saw a door. The door was open. Tom went in. The door closed. The door was locked. Tom was scared. He cried for help. The family did not come back. Tom was all alone.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the snow. They had cheap mittens that their mom had bought from the store. The mittens were red and blue and had holes in them. One day, they decided to make a snowman in their backyard. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot, a hat and a scarf to decorate their snowman. They were very happy with their work. "Look, our snowman is so nice!" Lily said. "Yes, he is! But he needs something else," Ben said. "What does he need?" Lily asked. "He needs mittens, like us!" Ben said. "But we only have two mittens, and they are not good," Lily said. "That's okay, we can share them with him," Ben said. He took off his blue mitten and spread it over the snowman's left hand. He asked Lily to do the same with her red mitten. They put their mittens on the snowman's right hand. "There, now he has mittens too!" Ben said. "But now our hands are cold," Lily said. They hugged each other and ran inside the house. Their mom saw them and smiled. "You made a snowman! He looks very cute with your mittens," she said. She gave them hot chocolate and new mittens that she had knitted for them. They were warm and soft and had no holes in them. "Thank you, mom! We love our new mittens!" Lily and Ben said. They drank their hot chocolate and put on their new mittens. They went back outside to play with their snowman. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals in the woods. They were friends and liked to play together. One day, they decided to make a big pot of soup for everyone to share. The little mouse was very good at stirring the soup. He used a big spoon and stirred it round and round. The soup began to smell very yummy. The other animals watched and waited for the soup to be ready. While they were waiting, a fierce wind came and blew the soup away. The animals were sad, but they knew they could make more soup together. So they did, and they all enjoyed the warm soup on a windy day.

One day, a girl named Amy wanted to bake a cake. She asked her mom, "Can we bake a cake today?" Her mom said, "Yes, but we need money to buy the things we need." Amy and her mom went to the store and bought all the things to make the perfect cake. When they got home, they started to bake the cake. They mixed all the things in a big bowl. They put the mix in the oven and waited for the cake to bake. Amy was very excited to see her perfect cake. But, when they opened the oven, they saw that the cake was not perfect. It was very big and looked funny. Amy was sad, but her mom said, "It's okay. We can still eat the cake and it will taste good." They laughed and ate the funny cake together. It was not perfect, but it was still yummy.

Once upon a time there was a curious little boy named Jack. He liked to explore the world around him, and one day he decided to climb up the chimney. With much effort, he was able to get right to the top. He was so proud of himself that he shouted "I did it". Suddenly, an old, tough voice interrupted him. "What are you doing up there? You could get hurt!" Jack looked down and saw an old man at the bottom of the chimney. The man said he'd been reading a book in his garden when he heard Jack's voice. Jack was too scared to answer, so he simply stayed at the top. The old man said he shouldn't be up there, and Jack began to feel scared. He wanted to get down, but he was too afraid to move. The old man gave him some tough advice. He said, "If you want to get down, you have to take one step at a time." Jack felt brave again, so he followed the old man’s advice. He carefully climbed down until his feet hit the ground. The old man smiled and asked if Jack was okay. Jack said he was, and thanked the old man for his help.

Once upon a time there was a chubby woman. She was walking through the park one day and spotted a muddy puddle. The woman started to wash her shoes in the puddle when a three year old walked up to her. The child said, “What are you doing?” The woman smiled and said, “Washing my shoes.” The child then exclaimed, “No, you can’t do that! That's my puddle!” The chubby woman tried to explain that she needed her shoes to be clean but the child was adamant. The woman was determined to get her shoes clean and started to argue with the child. After what felt like forever the woman finally convinced the child to let her wash her shoes. The chubby woman thanked the child and continued on her way with her freshly clean shoes. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. Joe was only three years old and loved to explore. One day, Joe went to the beach with his parents. It was a beautiful sunny day. When Joe arrived at the beach, he was so excited. He wanted to choose what he wanted to do first. Joe looked around and saw a reef in the water. He wanted to check it out! Joe's parents helped him put on his floaties and he jumped into the water. As he swam closer to the reef, he saw all sorts of colourful fish swimming around. He was also surprised to feel so many tiny, spicy sea creatures tickling his toes. Joe's parents asked him if he wanted to stay and explore the reef a bit more or swim back to the shore. Joe looked around and said "I choose to stay, I want to explore the reef and find more spicy sea creatures!" Joe's parents smiled and told him to be safe. Joe had an amazing time that day!

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. They want to go on the slide. "Let's go on the slide!" Lily says. "OK!" Tom says. They rush to the slide. They see a man with a mask. The mask is scary. It has big teeth and wide eyes. The man is bad. He wants to take Lily and Tom. "Help!" Lily and Tom shout. But no one hears them. The man grabs them. He puts them in a big bag. He runs away with the bag. Lily and Tom are sad and scared. They cry in the bag. They do not know where the man is taking them. They wish they did not go on the slide. They wish they stayed with their moms.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump together. The cat was fast, and the dog was strong. They were good friends. The cat said, "Let's pause and tell a joke." The dog sat down and said, "Okay, I have a joke. Why did the chicken cross the road?" The cat thought for a moment and said, "I don't know. Why did the chicken cross the road?" The dog laughed and said, "To get to the other side!" Suddenly, they saw a dead bug on the ground. The cat and the dog looked at it and felt sad. They decided to give the bug a nice place to rest. They dug a small hole and put the bug inside. Then they covered it with dirt and put a flower on top. After that, the cat and the dog went back to playing. They ran and jumped and had lots of fun. They knew they had done a good thing for the bug, and it made them happy.

Mummy and Daddy were walking in the park one day when they saw a baby. The baby had bright eyes and was wearing a little hat. Mummy and Daddy waved to the baby and the baby waved back with a big smile. The baby had a ball and it started to roll into a pool of water. Mummy and Daddy ran over to the baby and they all laughed when they saw the ball was wet. Then Daddy picked up the ball and threw it back to the baby. The baby was so happy and it waved again with a big smile. Mummy and Daddy waved back at the baby and were so pleased to see the baby so happy. They all kept waving until the baby went home.

Once upon a time, there was a famous lawyer. He was very good at his job. One day, he went to the park to play. He saw a big dog near a small cat. The dog was about to chase the cat. The famous lawyer said, "Dog, I warn you, do not chase the cat. It is not nice." The dog looked at him and said, "Okay, I will not chase the cat." Then, something unexpected happened. The cat jumped on the dog and they started to play! The famous lawyer was very surprised. He thought they would be scared of each other. But they were friends! The famous lawyer was happy to see them play together. And from that day on, the famous lawyer, the dog, and the cat were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a mild, sunny day, a boy named Tom went for a walk. He wanted to see a nice view from the top of a small hill. Tom was very happy and excited. He walked and walked until he reached the top. At the top of the hill, Tom saw a big tree. In the tree, there was a bird. The bird was singing a beautiful song. Tom liked the song, but he wanted to see the view. The bird was in his way. He asked the bird, "Please, bird, can you move? I want to see the view." The bird did not want to move. It just kept singing. Tom felt sad and a little mad. He thought of a plan. Tom took a big leaf and he gave the bird a little slap. The bird flew away, and Tom could finally see the view. Tom looked at the view and smiled. It was so pretty! The sky was blue, the sun was shining, and the grass was green. Tom felt happy again. He knew he should say sorry to the bird. So, he said, "Sorry, bird. I just wanted to see the view." The bird came back and sang again. Tom and the bird were friends, and they enjoyed the view together.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a grumpy dog named Max. Max liked to carry things in his mouth. One day, Max's owner, a nice lady, asked him to help her. "Max," she said, "please carry this newspaper to our neighbor, Mr. Brown." Max wagged his tail and took the newspaper in his mouth. Max walked down the street with the newspaper. On his way, he saw a cat. The cat was also grumpy. "Why are you carrying that newspaper?" the cat asked. Max just wagged his tail and kept walking. When Max gave the newspaper to Mr. Brown, he was very happy. "Thank you, Max!" he said with a big smile. Max wagged his tail and felt proud that he could help. From that day on, Max was not a grumpy dog anymore. He loved to carry things and help people in his town. Everyone loved Max, and he was a very happy dog.

Once upon a time there was a family who was very excited because they were going to take a plane for the first time. They were going to fly to see their grandparents, and could not wait to get on the plane. When the family arrived at the airport, they were surprised to see a fog had rolled in. The fog was so thick it was hard to see. The man behind the counter at the airport said they could not go on the plane because it was too dangerous. The family was very sad. The mom said, “We were so excited to take the plane and now we can’t go.” The dad said, “I have an idea. Let’s call Grandma and Grandpa and tell them what happened. Maybe we can think of something else.” So the dad called Grandma and Grandpa and explained the situation. Grandma had an idea. She said, “Why don’t you bring some sour candy for the flight attendants? We know they love sour candy! Then maybe they will take you on the plane.” The family thought it was a great idea, so they bought a big bag of sour candy. Sure enough, when they gave the candy to the flight attendants, they said they could take the plane! The family was so excited they cheered and laughed. The plane flew them to Grandma and Grandpa’

Once upon a time, in a big pond, there lived a green crocodile named Coco. Coco had many friends, but he was jealous of a big tree that could shake its leaves. Coco wished he could shake like the tree. One day, Coco's friend, a small bird named Chirpy, saw Coco looking sad. Chirpy asked, "Coco, why are you sad?" Coco said, "I am jealous of the big tree. It can shake its leaves, and I can't shake like that." Chirpy thought for a moment and said, "Coco, you can shake your big tail. It's just like shaking leaves!" Coco smiled and started to shake his tail. All his friends came to see Coco shake his tail. They clapped and cheered for Coco, and he was not jealous anymore. From that day on, Coco was happy to shake his big tail with all his friends around the pond.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a row of pretty flowers. Tim's mom told him to kneel down and smell the flowers. Tim did as his mom said. As Tim was smelling the flowers, he saw a big, stupid bug. The bug was green and had big eyes. Tim was scared and jumped back. He thought the bug would bite him. But then, the bug started to dance! Tim laughed and clapped his hands. The bug was not scary after all. It was a funny, dancing bug. Tim and his mom had a fun day at the park with their new friend.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy liked to pretend a lot. One day she was pretending to be a cook and decided to make some meat for dinner. She mixed together some ingredients and put it in a pot. She added some water and put it on the fire. It started to smell good! But when Lucy tasted her special dish she was very miserable. The meat tasted bad and wasn't cooked. She started to cry and said to herself, "I am a bad cook." Lucy was so disappointed but she still had hope. The next day, Lucy went to the store and bought some real meat. This time she was careful to make sure it was cooked properly. When the meat was ready, Lucy tasted it and she was so happy! The meat was delicious and she smiled from ear to ear. From then on, Lucy always remembers to pretend carefully and to always cook her meat properly.

Once upon a time there was a Mama and a Baby. Mama and Baby were having a nice day and went for a walk. Baby saw an oat in the snow and wanted to have it. But when Baby reached for the oat, it was icy cold. Mama said "No Baby, don't touch it. That is too cold." Baby said, "Please Mama, I want it." Mama said "No Baby, maybe another time." But Baby said he wanted it so Mama gave him the icy oat. Baby bit into the oat and it was cold and hard. He wanted a kiss from Mama to make it better. Mama said "No Baby, that won't help." But Baby begged so Mama gave Baby a kiss. But Baby's oat was still cold and hard. He was sad. Baby cried and it was a very bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. Sam loved to match things. He would match socks, toys, and even his snacks. One day, Sam found a rare, shiny rock. He wanted to find another one to match it. Sam looked everywhere for a rock to match his rare, shiny rock. He looked in his room, in the yard, and even at the park. But he couldn't find a match. Sam felt sad. Then, Sam's mom gave him an idea. She said, "Why don't you use ice to match your rare, shiny rock?" Sam thought this was a great idea. He went to the freezer and took out a piece of ice. The ice was shiny, just like his rock. Sam was happy because he found a match for his rare, shiny rock. But soon, the ice started to melt. Sam felt sad again. Sam's mom saw him and said, "Don't worry, Sam. You can always get more ice from the freezer to match your rock." Sam smiled and knew that he could always find a match for his rare, shiny rock with ice. And he lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was John. One day, John was walking along and he saw a jail. It was cheap and old. John wanted to go inside, so he carefully slipped through the door. John started exploring the jail, but it was dark and scary. He couldn't find his way out. John started to get scared. He started to cry. Suddenly, a friendly policeman came to help John. He told the boy how to slip out of the jail, back into the bright and sunny world. John thanked the policeman and went back home. John had a fun adventure, but he knew from then on to never slip into a jail again!

One day, a big cat and a small dog were in a park. The cat said, "Stay here with me, dog." The dog said, "Okay, cat. I will stay with you." They played with a wide ball. They had lots of fun. They ran and jumped. The cat was very fast, and the dog was very happy. Then, something unexpected happened. A bird came and took the wide ball. The cat and the dog looked at each other. They put their heads together and made a plan. The cat climbed a tree, and the dog barked at the bird. The bird got scared and dropped the wide ball. The cat and the dog got their ball back and were very happy. They played together and stayed friends.

Ben and Lily are friends who like to play with their dogs. Ben has a big dog named Max, and Lily has a small dog named Dot. One day, they go to the park with their dogs and their moms. They see a big field with many flowers and trees. Ben and Lily want to run and explore with their dogs, so they ask their moms if they can take off their leashes. Their moms say yes, but they tell them to stay close and to call their dogs if they go too far. Ben and Lily agree and take off their leashes. They run and laugh with their dogs, who chase each other and sniff the flowers. They have a lot of fun, but they don't notice that they are going very far from their moms. Suddenly, Ben hears his mom call his name. He looks up and sees her waving at him from a distant bench. He also sees that Max is nowhere to be seen. He feels scared and worried. He calls Max, but he doesn't hear him bark. He runs to his mom and tells her that he can't find Max. His mom hugs him and tells him not to worry. She says they will find him together. She takes his hand and they walk around the field, calling Max. Lily also hears her mom call her name. She looks up and sees her smiling at her from a distant bench. She also sees that Dot is right next to her, wagging her tail. She feels happy and proud. She calls Dot, and he comes to her. She puts his leash on and runs to her mom. She tells her mom that she had a lot of fun with Dot, and that he listened to her when she called him. Her mom praises her and tells her that she is a good dog owner. She hugs her and they sit on the bench, waiting for Ben and his mom. Soon, they see Ben and his mom walking towards them, with Max following behind. Ben looks relieved and happy. He tells them that he found Max in a bush, where he was chasing a squirrel. He says he is sorry for losing him, and that he will be more careful next time. His mom tells him that she is glad he is safe, and that he learned his lesson. She hugs him and they join Lily and her mom on the bench. The four of them chat and share some snacks, while their dogs rest and lick their faces. They enjoy the sunny day and the company of their friends. They decide to come back to the park again, but to keep their dogs on their leashes. They agree that it is more fun and safe that way.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk with her mom. They walked in the park and saw a big tree. Lucy said, "Mom, I want to sit under the tree." Her mom said, "Okay, let's sit there." As they walked to the tree, Lucy saw a big, wet puddle. Lucy wanted to jump in the puddle, but her mom said, "Be careful, Lucy. You might slip." Lucy listened and walked around the puddle. They sat under the tree and felt very comfortable. The tree gave them shade from the sun. Lucy looked at her mom and said, "I like sitting here with you, mom." Her mom smiled and said, "I like sitting here with you too, Lucy."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pale toy bear that she loved very much. She took it with her everywhere she went. One day, Lily and her bear went to the park to play. They ran, jumped, and laughed together. But then, Lily dropped her bear on the ground. She was very sad and didn't know what to do. A nice boy saw Lily crying and picked up the bear. He gave it back to her with a big smile. Lily felt happy again and hugged her bear tight. She thanked the boy and they played together all day. From that day on, Lily and the boy became best friends, and they shared their love for toys and fun.

Once upon a time, there was a poor, little fish. He lived in a big pond. The fish had a tiny house made of rocks. He had no friends because he was shy. One day, the little fish saw a shiny hook. The hook was hanging from a tree. The fish wanted to own the shiny hook. He thought, "I will make it my friend." The little fish swam up to the hook and said, "Hi, I am a fish. Will you be my friend?" The hook did not talk, but the fish did not mind. He was happy to have a friend. The fish and the hook played all day. They swam in the water and jumped over rocks. The fish was not poor and shy anymore. He had a friend, and that made him happy. And so, the little fish and the hook were best friends. They played together every day. The little fish was never alone again.

One day, a dove was flying in the sky. The dove saw a big tree and thought it would be a good place to rest. So, the dove flew down and sat on a branch. A crazy cat saw the dove and wanted to catch it. The cat climbed the tree very fast. The dove saw the cat and was scared. The cat jumped at the dove and tried to grab it. But, the branch the cat was on went "snap!" The cat fell down from the tree and landed on a soft pile of leaves. The dove flew away, safe and happy. The cat was not hurt, but it learned not to chase doves anymore.

One day, a big cake was made for two friends, Tom and Sue, to share. They wanted to have a fair share of the cake. They tried to separate the cake into two parts. But it was hard to do. So, they asked their friend, Max, for help. Max had a plan. He told Tom and Sue to close their eyes. They did, and Max took the cake away. Tom and Sue were sad when they opened their eyes and saw no cake. Max came back with two plates. On each plate, there was a piece of cake. Max had cut the cake into two fair parts. Tom and Sue were happy and said thank you. The moral of the story is that friends help each other and share.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous dog named Max. Max had a big itch on his back. He tried to scratch it, but his legs were too short. One day, Max saw a cat named Lily. Lily was very good at scratching her itches. Max asked Lily for help. "Can you help me with my itch, please?" Max said. Lily agreed to help Max. They became good friends. Max and Lily played a game called "match." They matched different toys and colors. Max was very happy. His itch was gone, and he had a new friend. They played and laughed all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Kitty. She had an owner who loved her very much. The owner liked to set a big bowl of food for Kitty every day. Kitty was very happy living with her owner. One day, the owner set a new toy for Kitty to play with. It was a big, red ball. Kitty loved to chase the ball around the house. She would run and jump and try to catch the ball. The owner would laugh and clap as Kitty played with the ball. As time went by, Kitty played with the ball every day. She became less fat and more strong. The owner was very happy to see Kitty healthy and having fun. They lived happily together, playing with the big, red ball.

One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue went to play near a big river. They saw a raft near the water. Tim said, "Let's play on the raft!" Sue agreed, and they both got on the raft. They were happy to display their new toy to their friends. As they played, the raft began to move. It went into the deep part of the river. Tim and Sue were scared. They did not know what to do. They called for help, but no one could hear them. Then, a big fish jumped out of the water. The fish saw the children and said, "Do not be scared. I will push the raft back to the shallow part of the river." Tim and Sue were surprised that the fish could talk, but they were happy for the help. The fish pushed the raft, and soon Tim and Sue were back near the land. They thanked the fish and went home to tell their friends about the talking fish who saved them.

Once upon a time there was a clean flame. It sparkled and shone in the night sky. All the animals wanted to join it in the dark. First, the dogs joined it. They barked and yipped as they ran around it. Then, the cats came and meowed. Finally, the birds flew down from the sky and perched on top. Together, the animals all looked so happy around the flame. They all jumped around and danced, enjoying the warmth of the fire. Then they heard a loud noise and they scattered, leaving the flame by itself. But soon they came back and joined it again. From then on, the flame and the animals were the best of friends. They were happy together and danced through the night every night.

One day, a big dog and a little cat were playing in the park. The dog had a smooth ball. The cat wanted to play with the ball too. But the dog did not want to share it. The cat said, "Please, can I play with the ball?" The dog did not listen to the cat's voice. The dog just kept playing with the ball. The cat felt sad. The cat decided to look for a new toy. It found a big, smooth stick. The dog saw the stick and wanted to play with it. The cat said, "We can share the stick and the ball." The dog agreed, and they played together happily.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. Tim saw a big oak tree and wanted to play near it. He was restless and could not wait to have fun. Tim saw a slide next to the oak tree. He climbed up and slid down the slide with a big smile on his face. He did this many times, laughing and having fun. But then, something unexpected happened. As Tim slid down the slide one more time, the oak tree started to shake. The tree was not really a tree, but a big, friendly giant! The giant stood up and asked Tim if he wanted to play. Tim and the giant played together all day, and Tim had the best day at the park ever.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a magic lamp. It was shiny and pretty. Tim took the lamp home and showed it to his mom. "Look, Mom! I found a lamp!" he said. His mom said, "Wow! That's a nice lamp, Tim." She put the lamp on a table. Tim looked at the lamp and saw a button. He pushed the button and the lamp started to turn. It turned fast and made Tim feel dizzy. Tim called his friend, Sam, to see the lamp. Sam came over and said, "Wow, that's a cool lamp!" Tim showed Sam how the lamp could turn. They both watched the lamp turn and felt dizzy. They laughed and played with the lamp all day.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet dog named Spot. Spot liked to spend his days playing in the park. He would run, jump, and roll in the grass. Spot was very happy. One day, Spot saw a girl named Jane. Jane was on a jog in the park. Spot wanted to play with Jane, so he ran up to her. Jane saw Spot and smiled. Jane and Spot spent the day together. They jogged and played in the park. They had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, Jane gave Spot a big hug. Spot was very happy to have a new friend.

One day, a polite duck named Ducky went for a walk by the lake. Ducky loved to swim in the lake and play with his friends. The sun was shining and the water was nice and cool. Ducky saw a big tree by the lake and thought it would be fun to play hide and seek with his friends. Ducky called out, "Hey, friends! Let's play hide and seek!" All his friends, like Froggy and Fishy, got excited and wanted to play too. Ducky closed his eyes and started to count. His friends ran and hid behind rocks, trees, and in the water. When Ducky finished counting, he started to look for his friends. He saw a little tail peek out from behind a rock. "I found you, Fishy!" he said. Fishy laughed and joined Ducky to find the others. They saw some legs peek out from under a leaf. "There you are, Froggy!" Ducky said. Froggy hopped out and smiled. After they found all their friends, they all played in the lake together. They splashed and swam until the sun started to go down. They knew it was time to go home. Ducky and his friends said goodbye and went to their homes. They couldn't wait to play again the next day.

One day, in a small town, a big dog named Max saw a little cat. The cat was lost and did not know where to go. Max wanted to help the cat, so he said, "Come with me. I will show you the town." Max and the cat walked around the town. They saw big trees, a park, and a clear blue sky. They played and had fun. The cat was happy to see the town with Max. Then, something unexpected happened. The little cat started to talk like a person! The cat said, "Thank you, Max. I am not a real cat. I am a magic cat. I was lost, but you helped me. Now, I will give you a gift." And with a wave of her tail, the magic cat made it so Max could talk like a person too. Now, Max and the magic cat could talk and play together all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max had a very important job. He had to deliver a towel to his friend, Cat. Max was ready to go on his long walk to Cat's house. On his way, Max met a little bird. The bird said, "Hi Max! Where are you going?" Max told the bird about his job to deliver the towel. The bird wanted to help Max, but Max said, "No, thank you. I can do it." As Max walked, he saw something he did not expect. It was a big, wet puddle. Max did not want the towel to get wet. So, he thought of a plan. He put the towel on his back and jumped over the puddle. But, the towel fell into the water! Max was sad. He could not deliver the wet towel to Cat now. But then, the little bird came back. The bird said, "I can help you, Max. I will fly and get a new towel for you." Max was happy and said, "Thank you, bird!" The bird flew away and came back with a new towel. Together, Max and the bird delivered the towel to Cat. They were all very happy.

One day, a large year came. There was a river nearby, and the water was so clear that you could see the bottom. When the people saw the river, they all decided to dive. Everyone was so excited. The first person was so brave. He jumped in and dove deep into the water. The second person was scared, but she mustered up enough courage to dive. It was so much fun. But when the third person dove into the river, something went wrong. No one knew what happened, but before anyone could help, he had disappeared from sight. Everyone was very sad. They knew the large year had ended with a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to bake yummy treats for her friends. One sunny day, Kitty decided to bake a big cake for everyone to share. Kitty put all the ingredients in a big bowl and mixed them up. She poured the mix into a cake tin and put it in the oven to bake. While the cake was baking, Kitty cleaned up the mess and threw the trash in the bin. When the cake was ready, Kitty took it out of the oven and let it cool. She decorated the cake with pretty colors and shared it with her friends. They all loved the cake and had a fun time eating it together. And from that day on, Kitty was known as the best baker in town.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. In the park, he saw a big bird. It was an ostrich. The ostrich looked at Tim and said, "Hi! I am Ollie the ostrich. Do you want to play with me?" Tim was happy to see Ollie. They played tag and hide and seek. After playing, Tim felt hungry. He took out a sour apple from his bag. He gave half of it to Ollie. They both ate the sour apple and made funny faces. Then, Ollie saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it. Tim said, "No, Ollie. It is not safe." But Ollie did not listen. He climbed the tree and fell down. Ollie was hurt and cried. Tim felt sad for Ollie. The moral of the story is to always listen to your friends when they tell you something is not safe.

Once upon a time there was a mule named Flip. He lived on a farm and every day he shined in the sun. He was strong and very easy to take care of. One day, Flip was in the barn eating hay when he heard a voice from outside. "Hello, Flip!" it said. Flip peeked out of the barn to see his old friend Sam. Sam smiled and said, "Would you like to come outside with me and play? The sun is shining and the day is so nice!" Flip was so excited and he followed Sam outside. They ran around the farm, playing tag. Then they went over to the garden and found a patch of grass to lie down on. It was so peaceful and easy. They stayed there until the sun set and the stars shone in the sky. Then Flip said goodbye to Sam and went back to the barn. The next day, Flip and Sam played outside in the sunshine again. It was always easy and fun!

One day, a mom and her three-year-old daughter went to the mall. The mom wanted to buy a sweater for her daughter. She said, "This mall is dependable. We can always get what we need here." They passed the stores, looking for the perfect sweater. Suddenly, the daughter saw a giant toy in the store window. She wanted it bad. "Mommy, can I get it?" She asked. But the mom said no. The daughter got angry and ran away. The mom ran after her daughter, but she couldn't find her anywhere. She searched and searched until it was dark. She asked people around the mall if they had seen her daughter, but no one had. She started to worry. The next day, the police said they had found the daughter. But she was safe in a different town. The mom had to wait a long time before she was finally reunited with her daughter. But this time, the mom was more careful and dependable.

One day, a bunny named Bob wanted to spring high. He wanted to touch the sky. He had a dream to win a trophy for the highest spring. Bob went to a clean park to practice. He saw a big tree and thought, "If I can spring to the top of the tree, I can win the trophy!" So, he tried and tried, but he could not spring high enough to touch the top of the tree. Just then, a little bird flew down and said, "I can help you, Bob!" The bird picked Bob up and took him to the top of the tree. Bob was so happy! But when they got to the top, they found a trophy already there. The trophy was for the best helper. Bob realized that the true trophy was not for the highest spring, but for helping others. He thanked the little bird and they became best friends. From that day on, Bob and the bird helped others together, and they were both very happy.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah. She was three years old. She got a costume for her birthday. It was a very special costume. It was a princess dress with lots of sparkles. One day Sarah was playing in her bedroom. She put the costume on and twirled around the room. Suddenly, Sarah heard somebody speak. She peeked behind her and saw a fairy. The fairy said, "Good afternoon Sarah! I have a secret to tell you." Sarah was quiet and excited. She said, "What is it?" The fairy said, "You must keep it a secret! You have magic powers now." Sarah smiled. She was amazed. The fairy said Goodbye and Sarah ran off to show her mom her new costume. She never told anyone the fairy's secret.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful king. He liked to sit on his big chair every day. The king had many friends in his kingdom. They all loved to play with him. One day, while the king was sitting on his chair, a small bird came to visit. The bird said, "Hello, King! Can I sit with you?" The king was very happy and said, "Of course! Come sit with me, little bird." They sat together and talked about fun things. But then, something unexpected happened! The bird changed into a big dragon! The king was scared, but the dragon said, "Do not be scared, King. I am your friend, too." The king was surprised but happy. They all played together and had a great day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a sweet old lady. She had a cane that she used to walk. One day, she went to the park with her cane. At the park, she met a little girl. The little girl said, "Hello! Can you bring me a flower?" The sweet old lady said, "Yes, I can bring you a flower. Wait here." The sweet old lady walked with her cane to find a flower. She saw a big, pretty flower. She thought, "This flower will make the little girl happy." She picked the flower with her cane. She brought the flower back to the little girl. The little girl was very happy. She said, "Thank you for the flower!" The sweet old lady smiled and said, "You're welcome!" They both had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old and she loved to explore. One day, she decided to go on an adventure in her backyard. As soon as she stepped outside, she saw a special box. She was so curious so she opened it. Inside, there was a big bag of white powder. It looked like snow! Lily scooped some of the powder with her hands and threw it up into the air. It started to float in the air like a cloud. She was so excited. It wasn't long before her mom came outside. She was angry. She saw the mess of powder on the ground. "Lily, why did you open that box?" her mom asked, in a stern voice. Lily just smiled and said, "Because it was fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat jelly. He liked all kinds of jelly, but his favorite was red jelly. One day, Tim saw a new kind of jelly in the store. It was different from what he had ever seen before. It was blue! Tim asked his mom, "Can we buy the blue jelly, please?" His mom said, "Sure, let's try something different today." Tim was so excited to taste the blue jelly. When they got home, Tim's mom put the blue jelly on a plate for him. As Tim took a bite, he heard a tiny whisper. He looked around and saw a little blue jelly friend! The jelly friend whispered, "Hi, Tim! I'm your new friend, Blue. We can play together!" Tim smiled and whispered back, "Hi, Blue! I'm happy to have a new friend!" From that day on, Tim and Blue had lots of fun together. They would always remember the day they met over a plate of different blue jelly.

One day, a grumpy car named Carl was driving down the road. Carl was always grumpy because he did not have enough fuel. He wanted to go fast and far, but he could not. Carl would always have to leave his friends behind when they went on trips. One day, Carl saw a big truck on the road. The big truck was carrying fuel. Carl had an idea. He thought if he could get some fuel from the truck, he would not be grumpy anymore. He followed the truck and waited for the right time. Then, something unexpected happened. The truck stopped and the driver got out. He saw Carl looking sad and asked, "Why are you so grumpy, little car?" Carl told him about his fuel problem. The driver smiled and said, "I have an idea!" He gave Carl some fuel from the truck. Now Carl was not grumpy anymore. He could go fast and far with his friends. But the plot twist was that the truck driver was Carl's long-lost brother. They were so happy to meet each other and promised to never leave each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Tim. Tim was an attractive bug with shiny wings. He liked to crawl around the garden and play with his friends. One day, Tim saw a big, tasty leaf on the ground. He wanted to eat it all by himself. Tim started to crawl towards the leaf. On his way, he met his friend, Sam the snail. Sam asked, "Tim, where are you going?" Tim said, "I am going to eat that big leaf over there." Sam looked at the leaf and said, "That looks yummy. Can I eat it with you?" Tim thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, Sam. We can share the leaf." Tim and Sam crawled together to the big leaf. They ate the leaf and had a great time. After they finished, Tim said, "I am glad we shared the leaf, Sam. It was more fun eating it with you." Sam agreed and said, "Sharing is always better than having something all by yourself." From that day on, Tim and Sam always shared their food with each other and their other friends in the garden. They learned that sharing makes everyone happy and it is more fun to enjoy things together. The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and it is more fun to enjoy things with friends.

Once upon a time, there was a young owl. She had big eyes and soft feathers. Every morning, she would rub her wings and look around. She loved the world around her! One day, she heard a voice calling her name. It was a young bird! He asked the owl to come and play. She was happy to join him, and soon the two of them were having lots of fun. The young owl liked to rub her wings against the bird's feathers. It felt so nice, and the bird loved it too! Every day, the two of them would go out to play, and the owl would rub her wings against the bird's feathers. The young owl and the young bird became great friends. They would go out together every day and have lots of fun. To this day, they can still be seen out in the open, playing together, and the owl will still rub her wings against the bird's feathers.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play in the park. One day, he saw a big, disgusting bug on the ground. He was scared but curious. He went closer to the bug and said, "Hello, bug! What are you doing?" The bug looked up at Tim and said, "Hello, Tim! I am making a plan to find food." Tim was surprised that the bug could talk. He decided to help the bug find food. They looked under rocks and in the grass. Then, something unexpected happened. Tim and the bug found a magic stone. The stone was shiny and pretty. Tim picked it up and suddenly, the bug turned into a beautiful butterfly. The butterfly said, "Thank you, Tim! The magic stone changed me back to my true self." Tim and the butterfly became best friends. They played in the park every day and had lots of fun. And they never saw the disgusting bug again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red armchair. The armchair was in a room with lots of toys. A little boy named Tim and his cat, Fluffy, loved to play in the room. One day, Tim's mommy said, "Tim, you can play in the room, but do not jump on the armchair." Tim was sad, but he said, "Okay, mommy." Tim and Fluffy played with the toys and had fun. After a while, Fluffy jumped on the armchair. Tim said, "No, Fluffy! Mommy will be angry." Fluffy jumped down and they played with the toys again. Tim and Fluffy had fun and did not jump on the armchair. They were happy because they listened to mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a nice bunny. The bunny loved to eat carrots. One sunny day, the bunny went to find a big carrot to eat. The bunny saw the biggest carrot ever! But it was on a hill. The bunny went up the hill to get the carrot. As the bunny got close, it started to slip. Just as the bunny was about to fall, a bird came and helped. The bird got the carrot for the bunny. The bunny and the bird became friends. They shared the big carrot and had a nice day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Tom. Tom loved collecting things his mum gave him. One day, Tom's mum told him to go and collect some rubber. Tom was so excited. He said to his mum, "But where will I find rubber?" His mum smiled and said, "Be creative, Tom. It's all around you. I'm sure you'll think of something!" Tom thought hard and decided that he could collect rubber by collecting rubber bands. So, he took a walk around his garden and found lots of rubber bands to collect. He was so proud of his collection and took it to show his mum. His mum said, "Oh, that's so creative, Tom. Well done!" Tom was so happy that he had been able to find and collect something from his garden.

Once upon a time, there was a selfish cat. The cat did not like to share with others. One day, a storm came to the town. The wind blew strong and the rain fell hard. In the storm, the cat saw a small bird who needed help. The bird was cold and wet. The cat thought, "I can change and help the bird." But the selfish cat did not want to share its warm and dry home. The storm got worse and the bird could not find a safe place. The cat watched the bird but did nothing. The storm was too strong for the bird, and it did not make it through the night. The selfish cat stayed warm and dry but felt sad and alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was John and he was three years old. John was at the playground with his friends, Sammy and Maria. He loved to rock in the rocking chair, but Maria wanted to go on the slide. John said, "No, I'm going to rock!" So John rocked in the chair until it went very fast. When it stopped, his clothes were all messed up. John started to laugh, but then he noticed something big, dark and scary across the playground. John said, "Who is that?" But his friends just shrugged and said, "We don't know." John was scared, but then the big scary thing came closer and he saw it was just a big black bird. He laughed and said, "That's not scary after all!" John and his friends continued to play, but making sure to take turns rocking in the chair.

One day, a wise old owl sat on a tree. He liked to give talks to the animals in the forest. These talks were called lectures. All the animals liked to listen to the wise owl's lectures. One day, the wise owl said to the animals, "I will give a lecture about sharing." All the animals came to listen. They sat down and looked at the wise owl. The wise owl started to talk. "Sharing is when you give something to someone else," he said. But then, something unexpected happened! A little mouse stood up and said, "I want to give a lecture too!" All the animals were surprised. They had never heard the little mouse talk before. The wise owl smiled and said, "Okay, little mouse. You can give a lecture too." So the little mouse gave a lecture about being brave. All the animals listened and learned from the wise owl and the brave little mouse.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big cross made of wood. It was near some flowers and trees. "Look, a cross!" Lily said. "Let's go and see it." They ran to the cross and touched it. It was hard and rough. "Maybe it is a fake cross," Tom said. "Maybe someone put it here for fun." He pushed the cross with his hand. It did not move. "See? It is real. It is stuck in the ground," Lily said. She pushed the cross too. It still did not move. They pushed harder and harder. They wanted to make the cross fall. But the cross was too strong. It did not fall. They heard a voice behind them. "Hey, what are you doing?" the voice said. They turned around and saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He looked angry. "This is my cross. I made it for my garden. It is not fake. It is not for playing. Stop pushing it!" the man said. Lily and Tom felt scared. They did not know the man. They did not know he owned the cross. They said sorry to the man. They ran away from the cross. They did not want to push it anymore. They went back to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She was reading a book. "Mom, we saw a cross in the park. It was real. A man made it for his garden. He was mad at us. We pushed it," Lily said. "Really? That was not nice of you. You should not push things that are not yours. You should respect other people's things. You should say sorry if you make a mistake," mom said. "We did say sorry, mom. We were just curious. We thought it was fake," Tom said. Mom hugged them and kissed them. "I know, my loves. You are still learning. But you have to be careful. Some things are not for playing. Some things are special to someone. You have to ask before you touch them. You have to be polite and kind," mom said. Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They felt sorry for the man and his cross.
